1.1: Now the Lord called Moses, and spake unto him out of the Tabernacle of the Congregation, saying,
1.2: Speak unto the children of Israel, and thou shalt say unto them, If any of you offer a sacrifice unto the Lord, ye shall offer your sacrifice of cattell, as of beeves and of the sheep.
1.3: If his sacrifice be a burnt offering of the heard, he shall offer a male without blemish, presenting him of his own voluntarie will at the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation before the Lord.
1.4: And he shall put his hand upon the head of the burnt offering, and it shalbe accepted to the Lord, to be his atonement.
1.5: And he shall kill the bullock before the Lord, and the Priestes Aarons sonnes shall offer the blood, and shall sprinckle it round about upon the altar, that is by the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation.
1.6: Then shall he fley the burnt offering, and cut it in pieces.
1.7: So the sonnes of Aaron the Priest shall put fire upon the altar, and lay the wood in order upon the fire.
1.8: Then the Priestes Aarons sonnes shall lay the parts in order, the head and the kall upon the wood that is in the fire which is upon the altar.
1.9: But the inwardes thereof and the legges thereof he shall wash in water, and the Priest shall burn all on the altar: for it is a burnt offering, an oblation made by fire, for a sweet sauour unto the Lord.
1.10: And if his sacrifice for the burnt offering be of the flocks (as of the sheep, or of the goats) he shall offer a male without blemish,
1.11: And he shall kill it on the Northside of the altar before the Lord, and the Priestes Aarons sonnes shall sprinckle the blood thereof round about upon the altar.
1.12: And he shall cut it in pieces, separating his head and his kall, and the Priest shall lay them in order upon the wood that lyeth in the fire which is on the altar:
1.13: But he shall wash the inwardes, and the legges with water, and the Priest shall offer the whole and burn it upon the altar: for it is a burnt offering, an oblation made by fire for a sweet sauour unto the Lord.
1.14: And if his sacrifice be a burnt offring to the Lord of ye foules, then he shall offer his sacrifice of the turtle doves, or of the yong pigeons.
1.15: And the Priest shall bring it unto the altar, and wring the neck of it asunder, and burn it on the altar: and the blood thereof shall bee shed upon the side of the altar.
1.16: And he shall pluck out his maw with his fethers, and cast them beside the altar on the East part in the place of the ashes.
1.17: And he shall cleave it with his wings, but not deuide it asunder: and the Priest shall burn it upon the altar upon the wood that is in the fire: for it is a burnt offering, an oblation made by fire for a sweet sauour unto the Lord.

2.1: And when any will offer a meat offering unto the Lord, his offering shall be of fine flour, and he shall powre oyle upon it, and put incense thereon,
2.2: And shall bring it unto Aarons sonnes the Priestes, and he shall take thence his handful of the flowre, and of the oyle with al the incense, and the Priest shall burn it for a memorial upon the altar: for it is an offering made by fire for a sweet sauour unto the Lord.
2.3: But the remnant of the meat offering shalbe Aarons and his sonnes: for it is most holy of the Lordes offrings made by fire.
2.4: If thou bring also a meat offring baken in the oven, it shalbe an vnleauened cake of fine flour mingled with oyle, or an vnleauened wafer anointed with oyle.
2.5: But if thy meat offring be an oblation of the frying pan, it shall be of fine flowre vnleauened, mingled with oyle.
2.6: And thou shalt part it in pieces, and power oyle thereon: for it is a meat offring.
2.7: And if thy meat offring be an oblation made in the caldron, it shalbe made of fine flour with oyle.
2.8: After, thou shalt bring the meat offering (that is made of these things) unto the Lord, and shalt present it unto the Priest, and he shall bring it to the altar,
2.9: And the Priest shall take from the meat offring a memorial of it, and shall burn it upon the altar: for it is an oblation made by fire for a sweet sauour unto the Lord.
2.10: But that which is left of the meat offring, shalbe Aarons and his sonnes: for it is most holy of the offrings of the Lord made by fire.
2.11: All the meat offrings which ye shall offer unto the Lord, shalbe made without leaven: for ye shall neither burn leaven nor honie in any offring of the Lord made by fire.
2.12: In the oblation of the first fruits ye shall offer them unto the Lord, but they shall not be burnt upon the altar for a sweet sauour.
2.13: (All the meat offrings also shalt thou season with salt, neither shalt thou suffer the salt of the covenant of thy God to be lacking from thy meat offring, but upon all thine oblations thou shalt offer salt)
2.14: If then thou offer a meat offring of thy first fruites unto the Lord, thou shalt offer for thy meat offering of thy first fruites eares of corn dryed by the fire, and wheat beaten out of the green eares.
2.15: After, thou shalt put oyle upon it, and lay incense thereon: for it is a meat offring.
2.16: And the Priest shall burn the memorial of it, even of that that is beaten, and of the oyle of it, with all the incense thereof: for it is an offring unto the Lord made by fire.

3.1: Also if his oblation be a peace offering, if he will offer of the drove (whether it be male or female) he shall offer such as is without blemish, before the Lord,
3.2: And shall put his hand upon the head of his offering, and kill it at the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation: and Aarons sonnes the Priestes shall sprinkle the blood upon the altar round about.
3.3: So he shall offer part of the peace offerings as a sacrifice made by fire unto the Lord, even the fat that covereth the inwardes, and all the fat that is upon the inwardes.
3.4: He shall also take away the two kidneis, and the fat that is on them, and upon the flankes, and the kall on the liver with the kidneis.
3.5: And Aarons sonnes shall burn it on the altar, with the burnt offering, which is upon the wood, that is on the fire: this is a sacrifice made by fire for a sweet sauour unto the Lord.
3.6: Also if his oblation be a peace offring unto the Lord out of ye flock, whether it be male or female, he shall offer it without blemish.
3.7: If he offer a lamb for his oblation, then he shall bring it before the Lord,
3.8: And lay his hand upon the head of his offring, and shall kill it before the Tabernacle of the Congregation, and Aarons sonnes shall sprinckle the blood thereof round about upon the altar.
3.9: After, of the peace offrings he shall offer an offring made by fire unto the Lord: he shall take away the fat therof, and the rump altogether, hard by the back bone, and the fat that covereth the inwardes, and all the fat that is upon the inwards.
3.10: Also hee shall take away the two kidneis, with the fat that is upon them, and upon the flankes, and the kall upon the liver with the kidneis.
3.11: Then the Priest shall burn it upon the altar, as the meat of an offring made by fire unto the Lord.
3.12: Also if his offring be a goat, then shall he offer it before the Lord,
3.13: And shall put his hand upon the head of it, and kill it before the Tabernacle of the Congregation, and the sonnes of Aaron shall sprinkle the blood thereof upon the altar round about.
3.14: Then he shall offer thereof his offring, even an offring made by fire unto the Lord, the fat that covereth the inwardes, and all the fatte that is upon the inwardes.
3.15: Also hee shall take away the two kidneis, and the fat that is upon them, and upon ye flankes, and the kall upon the liver with the kidneis.
3.16: So the Priest shall burn them upon the altar, as the meat of an offering made by fire for a sweet sauour: all the fatte is the Lordes.
3.17: This shalbe a perpetual ordinance for your generations, throughout al your dwellings, so that ye shall eat neither fatte nor blood.

4.1: Moreover the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
4.2: Speak unto the children of Israel, saying, If any shall sinne through ignorance, in any of the commandementes of the Lord, (which ought not to be done) but shall doe contrary to any of them,
4.3: If the Priest that is anointed doe sinne (according to the sinne of the people) then shall he offer, for his sinne which hee hath sinned, a yong bullock without blemish unto the Lord for a sinne offring,
4.4: And hee shall bring the bullock unto the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation before the Lord, and shall put his hand upon the bullocks head, and kill the bullock before the Lord.
4.5: And the Priest that is anointed shall take of the bullocks blood, and bring it into the Tabernacle of the Congregation.
4.6: Then the Priest shall dippe his finger in the blood, and sprinkle of the blood seven times before the Lord, before the vail of the Sanctuarie.
4.7: The Priest also shall put some of the blood before the Lord, upon the hornes of the altar of sweet incense, which is in the Tabernacle of the Congregation, then shall hee powre all the rest of the blood of the bullock at the foot of the altar of burnt offring, which is at the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation.
4.8: And hee shall take away all the fat of the bullock for the sinne offring: to wit, the fat that covereth the inwardes, and all the fatte that is about the inwardes.
4.9: He shall take away also the two kidneis, and the fat that is upon them, and upon the flankes, and the kall upon the liver with the kidneis,
4.10: As it was taken away from the bullock of the peace offrings, and the Priest shall burn them upon the altar of burnt offring.
4.11: But the skinne of the bullock, and all his flesh, with his head, and his legs, and his inwardes, and his dung shall he bear out.
4.12: So he shall cary the whole bullock out of the host unto a clean place, where the ashes are powred, and shall burn him on ye wood in the fire: where ye ashes are cast out, shall he be burnt.
4.13: And if the whole Congregation of Israel shall sinne through ignorance, and the thing be hid from the eyes of the multitude, and have done against any of the commandements of the Lord which should not be done, and have offended:
4.14: When the sinne which they have committed shalbe knowen, then the Congregation shall offer a yong bullock for the sinne, and bring him before the Tabernacle of the Congregation,
4.15: And the Elders of the Congregation shall put their handes upon the head of the bullock before the Lord, and he shall kill the bullock before the Lord.
4.16: Then the Priest that is anointed, shall bring of the bullockes blood into the Tabernacle of the Congregation,
4.17: And the Priest shall dip his finger in the blood, and sprinkle it seven times before the Lord, even before the vail.
4.18: Also he shall put some of ye blood upon the hornes of the altar, which is before the Lord, that is in the Tabernacle of the Congregation: then shall he powre all the rest, of the blood at ye foot of the altar of burnt offring, which is at the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation,
4.19: And he shall take all his fat from him, and burn it upon the altar.
4.20: And the Priest shall doe with this bullock, as he did with the bullock for his sinne: so shall he do with this: so the Priest shall make an atonement for them, and it shalbe forgiven them.
4.21: For he shall carie the bullock without the host, and burn him as he burned the first bullock: for it is an offring for the sinne of the Congregation.
4.22: When a ruler shall sinne, and do through ignorance against any of the commandements of the Lord his God, which should not be done, and shall offend,
4.23: If one shew unto him his sinne, which he hath committed, the shall he bring for his offring an hee goat without blemish,
4.24: And shall lay his hand upon the head of the he goat, and kill it in the place where he should kill the burnt offring before the Lord: for it is a sinne offring.
4.25: Then the Priest shall take of the blood of the sinne offring with his finger, and put it upon the hornes of the burnt offring altar, and shall powre the rest of his blood at the foot of the burnt offring altar,
4.26: And shall burn all his fat upon the altar, as the fat of the peace offring: so the Priest shall make an atonement for him, concerning his sinne, and it shalbe forgiven him.
4.27: Likewise if any of the people of ye land shall sinne through ignoraunce in doing against any of the commandements of the Lord, which should not be done, and shall offend,
4.28: If one shew him his sinne which he hath committed, then he shall bring for his offring, a she goat without blemish for his sinne which he hath committed,
4.29: And he shall lay his hand upon the head of the sinne offring, and slay the sinne offring in the place of burnt offring.
4.30: Then the Priest shall take of the blood thereof with his finger, and put it upon the hornes of the burnt offring altar, and powre all the rest of the blood thereof at the foot of the altar,
4.31: And shall take away all his fat, as the fat of the peace offringes is taken away, and the Priest shall burn it upon the altar for a sweet sauour unto the Lord, and the Priest shall make an atonement for him, and it shalbe forgiven him.
4.32: And if he bring a lamb for his sinne offring, he shall bring a female without blemish,
4.33: And shall lay his hand upon the head of the sinne offring, and hee shall slay it for a sinne offring in the place where hee should kill the burnt offring.
4.34: Then the Priest shall take of the blood of the sinne offring with his finger, and put it upon the hornes of the burnt offring altar, and shall powre al the rest of the blood thereof at the foot of the altar.
4.35: And he shall take away all the fat thereof, as the fatte of the lamb of the peace offrings is taken away: then the Priest shall burn it upon the altar with the oblations of the Lord made by fire, and the Priest shall make an atonement for him concerning his sinne that he hath committed, and it shalbe forgiven him.

5.1: Also if any have sinned, that is, If he have heard the voyce of an othe, and hee can be a witnes, whether he hath seen or knowen of it, if hee doe not utter it, he shall bear his iniquitie:
5.2: Either if one touch any vncleane thing, whether it be a carion of an vncleane beast, or a carion of vncleane cattel, or a carion of vncleane creeping things, and is not ware of it, yet he is vncleane, and hath offended:
5.3: Eyther if hee touch any vncleannesse of man (whatsoever vncleannes it be, that hee is defiled with) and is not ware of it, and after cometh to the knowledge of it, he hath sinned:
5.4: Either if any swear and pronounce with his lippes to do evil, or to doe good (whatsoever it bee that a man shall pronounce with an othe) and it be hid from him, and after knoweth that he hath offended in one of these poyntes,
5.5: Whe he hath sinned in any of these things, then he shall confess that he hath sinned therein.
5.6: Therefore shall he bring his trespass offring unto the Lord for his sinne which he hath committed, even a female from ye flock, be it a lamb or a she goat for a sinne offring, and the Priest shall make an atonement for him, concerning his sinne.
5.7: But if he be not able to bring a sheep, he shall bring for his trespas which he hath committed, two turtle doves, or two yong pigeons unto the Lord, one for a sinne offring, and the other for a burnt offring.
5.8: So he shall bring them unto the Priest, who shall offer the sinne offring first, and wring the neck of it a sunder, but not pluck it clean off.
5.9: After he shall sprinkle of the blood of the sinne offring upon the side of the altar, and the rest of the blood shall be shed at the foot of the altar: for it is a sinne offering.
5.10: Also he shall offer the second for a burnt offring as the maner is: so shall the Priest make an atonement for him (for his sinne which hee hath committed) and it shalbe forgiven him.
5.11: But if he be not able to bring two turtle doves, or two yong pigeons, then he that hath sinned, shall bring for his offring, the tenth part of an Ephah of fine flour for a sinne offring, he shall put none oyle thereto, neither put any incense thereon: for it is a sinne offering.
5.12: Then shall hee bring it to the Priest, and the Priest shall take his handful of it for the remembrance thereof, and burn it upon the altar with the offrings of the Lord made by fire: for it is a sinne offring.
5.13: So the Priest shall make an atonement for him, as touching his sinne that he hath committed in one of these poyntes, and it shall bee forgiven him: and the remnant shalbe the Priests, as the meat offring.
5.14: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
5.15: If any person transgress and sinne through ignorance by taking away things consecrated unto the Lord, hee shall then bring for his trespass offring unto the Lord a ramme without blemish out of the flock, worth two shekels of silver by thy estimation after the shekel of the Sanctuarie, for a trespass offring.
5.16: So hee shall restore that wherein hee hath offended, in taking away of the holy thing, and shall put the fift part more thereto, and give it unto the Priest: so the Priest shall make an atonement for him with the ram of ye trespass offring, and it shalbe forgiven him.
5.17: Also if any sinne and doe against any of the commandements of the Lord, which ought not to be done, and know not and sinne and bear his iniquitie,
5.18: Then shall he bring a ramme without blemish out of the flock, in thy estimation worth two shekels for a trespass offring unto ye Priest: and the Priest shall make an atonement for him concerning his ignorance wherein he erred, and was not ware: so it shalbe forgiven him.
5.19: This is the trespass offring for the trespass committed against the Lord.

6.1: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
6.2: If any sinne and commit a trespass against the Lord, and denie unto his neighbour that, which was take him to keep, or that which was put to him of trust, or doth by robberie, or by violence oppress his neighbour,
6.3: Or hath found that which was lost, and denieth it, and sweareth falsely, for any of these things that a man doeth, wherein he sinneth:
6.4: When, I say, he thus sinneth and trespasseth, he shall then restore the robbery that he robbed, or the thing taken by violence which hee took by force, or the thing which was delivered him to keep, or the lost thing which he found,
6.5: Or for whatsoever he hath sworn falsely, he shall both restore it in the whole summe, and shall add the fift part more thereto, and give it unto him to whom perteyneth, the same day that he offreth for trespass.
6.6: Also he shall bring for his trespass unto the Lord, a ramme without blemish out of the flock in thy estimation worth two shekels for a trespass offring unto the Priest.
6.7: And the Priest shall make an atonement for him before the Lord, and it shall be forgiven him, whatsoever thing he hath done, and trespassed therein.
6.8: Then the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
6.9: Commaund Aaron and his sonnes, saying, This is the law of the burnt offring, (it is the burnt offring because it burneth upon the altar al the night unto the morning, and the fire burneth on the altar)
6.10: And the Priest shall put on his linen garment, and shall put on his linen breeches upon his flesh, and take away the ashes when the fire hath consumed the burnt offring upon the altar, and he shall put them beside the altar.
6.11: After, he shall put off his garments, and put on other raiment, and cary the ashes foorth without the host unto a clean place.
6.12: But the fire upon the altar shall burn thereon and never be put out: wherefore the Priest shall burn wood on it every morning, and lay the burnt offering in order upon it, and he shall burn thereon the fat of the peace offrings.
6.13: The fire shall ever burn upon the altar, and never go out.
6.14: Also this is the law of the meat offring, which Aarons sonnes shall offer in the presence of the Lord, before the altar.
6.15: He shall even take thence his handful of fine flowre of the meat offring and of the oyle, and all the incense which is upon the meat offring, and shall burn it upon the altar for a sweet sauour, as a memorial therefore unto the Lord:
6.16: But the rest thereof shall Aaron and his sonnes eat: it shalbe eaten without leaven in the holy place: in the court of the Tabernacle of the Congregation they shall eat it.
6.17: It shall not be baken with leaven: I have given it for their portion of mine offrings made by fire: for it is as the sinne offering and as the trespass offring.
6.18: All the males among the children of Aaron shall eat of it: It shalbe a statute for ever in your generations concerning the offrings of the Lord, made by fire: whatsoever toucheth them shall be holy.
6.19: Agayne the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
6.20: This is the offering of Aaron and his sonnes, which they shall offer unto the Lord in the day when he is anointed: the tenth part of an Ephah of fine flour, for a meat offering perpetual: half of it in ye morning, and half thereof at night.
6.21: In the frying panne it shalbe made with oyle: thou shalt bring it fryed, and shalt offer the baken pieces of the meat offering for a sweet sauour unto the Lord.
6.22: And the Priest that is anointed in his stead, among his sonnes shall offer it: It is the Lordes ordinance for ever, it shall be burnt altogether.
6.23: For every meat offring of the Priest shall be burnt altogether, it shall not be eaten.
6.24: Furthermore, the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
6.25: Speak unto Aaron, and unto his sonnes, and say, This is the Law of the sinne offering, In the place where the burnt offring is killed, shall the sinne offring be killed before the Lord, for it is most holy.
6.26: The Priest that offreth this sinne offring, shall eat it: in the holy place shall it be eaten, in the court of ye Tabernacle of the Congregation.
6.27: Whatsoever shall touch the flesh thereof shalbe holy: and when there droppeth of the blood thereof upon a garment, thou shalt wash that whereon it droppeth in the holy place.
6.28: Also the earthen pot that it is sodden in, shalbe broken, but if it be sodden in a brasen pot, it shall both be scoured and washed with water.
6.29: All the males among the Priestes shall eat thereof, for it is most holy.
6.30: But no sinne offering, whose blood is brought into the Tabernacle of the Congregation to make reconciliation in the holy place, shalbe eaten, but shalbe burnt in the fire.

7.1: Likewise this is the law of the trespass offering, it is most holy.
7.2: In the place where they kill the burnt offering, shall they kill the trespass offering, and the blood thereof shall he sprinkle round about upon the altar.
7.3: All the fat thereof also shall he offer, the rump, and the fat that covereth the inwardes.
7.4: After he shall take away the two kidneis, with the fat that is on them and upon the flankes, and the kall on the liver with the kidneis.
7.5: Then the Priest shall burn them upon the altar, for an offring made by fire unto the Lord: this is a trespass offring.
7.6: All the males among the Priestes shall eat thereof, it shalbe eaten in the holy place, for it is most holy.
7.7: As the sinne offring is, so is the trespass offring, one law serveth for both: that wherewith the Priest shall make atonement, shalbe his.
7.8: Also the Priest that offereth any mans burnt offring, shall have the skinne of the burnt offring which he hath offered.
7.9: And all the meat offring that is baken in the oven, and that is dressed in the pan, and in the frying pan, shall be the Priestes that offereth it.
7.10: And every meat offering mingled with oyle, and that is dry, shall pertain unto all the sonnes of Aaron, to all alike.
7.11: Furthermore, this is the law of the peace offrings, which he shall offer unto the Lord.
7.12: If he offer it to give thankes, then he shall offer for his thankes offering, vnleauened cakes mingled with oyle, and vnleauened wafers anointed with oyle, and fine flour fryed with the cakes mingled with oyle.
7.13: He shall offer also his offring with cakes of leavened bread, for his peace offrings, to give thankes.
7.14: And of all the sacrifice he shall offer one cake for an heave offering unto the Lord, and it shalbe the Priestes that sprinckleth the blood of the peace offrings.
7.15: Also the flesh of his peace offerings, for thankesgiuing, shalbe eaten the same day that it is offered: he shall leave nothing thereof until the morning.
7.16: But if the sacrifice of his offring be a vow, or a free offering, it shalbe eaten the same day that he offreth his sacrifice: and so in the morning the residue thereof shalbe eaten.
7.17: But as much of the offered flesh as remaineth unto the third day, shalbe burnt with fire.
7.18: For if any of the flesh of his peace offrings be eaten in the third day, he shall not be accepted that offereth it, neither shall it be reckoned unto him, but shalbe an abomination: therefore ye person that eateth of it shall bear his iniquitie.
7.19: The flesh also that toucheth any vncleane thing, shall not be eaten, but burnt with fire: but of this flesh all that be clean shall eat thereof.
7.20: But if any eat of the flesh of the peace offerings that pertaineth to the Lord, having his vncleannesse upon him, even the same person shalbe cut off from his people.
7.21: Moreover, whe any toucheth any vncleane thing, as the vncleannesse of man, or of an vncleane beast, or of any filthie abomination, and eat of the flesh of the peace offrings, which pertaineth unto the Lord, even that person shalbe cut off from his people.
7.22: Again ye Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
7.23: Speak unto the children of Israel, and say, Ye shall eat no fat of beeves, nor of sheep, nor of goates:
7.24: Yet the fat of the dead beast, and the fat of that, which is torn with beastes, shalbe occupied to any use, but ye shall not eat of it.
7.25: For whosoever eateth the fat of the beast, of the which he shall offer an offering made by fire to the Lord, even the person that eateth, shalbe cut off from his people.
7.26: Neither shall ye eat any blood, either of fowl, or of beast in all your dwellings.
7.27: Every person that eateth any blood, even the same person shall be cut off from his people.
7.28: And the Lord talked with Moses, saying,
7.29: Speak unto the children of Israel, and say, Hee that offereth his peace offerings unto the Lord, shall bring his gift unto the Lord of his peace offerings:
7.30: His handes shall bring the offerings of the Lord made by fire: even the fatte with the breast shall he bring, that the breast may be shaken to and from before the Lord.
7.31: Then the Priest shall burn the fatte upon the Altar, and the breast shall be Aarons and his sonnes.
7.32: And the right shoulder shall ye give unto the Priest for an heave offering, of your peace offrings.
7.33: The same that offreth the blood of ye peace offrings, and the fatte, among the sonnes of Aaron, shall have the right shoulder for his part.
7.34: For the breast shaken to and from, and the shoulder lifted up, have I taken of the children of Israel, even of their peace offrings, and have given them unto Aaron the Priest and unto his sonnes by a statute for ever from among the children of Israel.
7.35: This is the anointing of Aaron, and the anointing of his sonnes, concerning the offerings of the Lord made by fire, in the day when he presented them to serve in the Priestes office unto the Lord.
7.36: The which portions the Lord commanded to give them in the day that he anointed them from among the children of Israel, by a statute for ever in their generations.
7.37: This is also the law of the burnt offring of the meat offring, and of the sinne offring, and of the trespass offring, and of the consecrations, and of the peace offrings,
7.38: Which the Lord commanded Moses in the mount Sinai, when he commanded the children of Israel to offer their giftes unto the Lord in the wilderness of Sinai.

8.1: Afterward the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
8.2: Take Aaron and his sonnes with him, and the garments and the anointing oyle, and a bullock for the sinne offring, and two rammes, and a basket of vnleauened bread,
8.3: And assemble all the company at the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation.
8.4: So Moses did as the Lord had commanded him, and the companie was assembled at the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation.
8.5: Then Moses said unto the company, This is the thing which the Lord hath commanded to doe.
8.6: And Moses brought Aaron and his sonnes, and washed them with water,
8.7: And put upon him the coat, and girded him with a girdle, and clothed him with the robe, and put the Ephod on him, which he girded with the broydred garde of the Ephod, and bound it unto him therewith.
8.8: After he put the brest plate thereon, and put in the breast plate the Urim and the Thummim.
8.9: Also he put the miter upon his head, and put upon the miter on the for front the golden plate, and the holy crown, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
8.10: (Now Moses had taken the anointing oyle, and anoynted the Tabernacle, and al that was therein, and sanctified them,
8.11: And sprinkled thereof upon the altar seven times, and anointed the altar and all his instruments, and the laver, and his foot, to sanctifie them)
8.12: And he powred of the anointing oyle upon Aarons head, and anointed him, to sanctifie him.
8.13: After, Moses brought Aarons sonnes, and put coates upon them, and girded them with girdles, and put bonets upon their heades, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
8.14: Then he brought the bullock for the sinne offring, and Aaron and his sonnes put their handes upon the head of the bullock for the sinne offring.
8.15: And Moses slew him, and took the blood, which he put upon the hornes of the Altar roud about with his finger, and purified the altar, and powred the rest of the blood at the foot of ye altar: so he sanctified it, to make reconciliation upon it.
8.16: Then he took all the fatte that was upon the inwardes, and the kall of the liver and the two kidneis, with their fat, which Moses burned upon the Altar.
8.17: But the bullock and his hide, and his flesh, and his doung, hee burnt with fire without the host as the Lord had commanded Moses.
8.18: Also hee brought the ram for the burnt offring, and Aaron and his sonnes put their hands upon the head of the ramme.
8.19: So Moses killed it, and sprinkled the blood upon the Altar round about,
8.20: And Moses cut the ram in pieces, and burnt the head with the pieces, and the fat,
8.21: And washed the inwardes and the legges in water: so Moses burnt the ram every whit upon ye Altar: for it was a burnt offring for a sweet sauour, which was made by fire unto the Lord, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
8.22: After, he brought the other ram, the ram of consecrations, and Aaron and his sonnes layed their handes upon the head of the ram,
8.23: Which Moses slew, and took of the blood of it, and put it upon the lappe of Aarons right ear, and upon the thumb of his right hand, and upon the great toe of his right foot.
8.24: Then Moses brought Aarons sonnes, and put of the blood on the lap of their right eares, and upon the thumbes of their right handes, and upon the great toes of their right feet, and Moses sprinckled the rest of the blood upon the Altar round about.
8.25: And he took the fat and the rump and all the fat that was upon the inwards, and the kall of the liver, and the two kidneis with their fat, and the right shoulder.
8.26: Also he took of ye basket of ye vnleauened bread that was before the Lord, one vnleauened cake and a cake of oiled bread, and one wafer, and put them on the fat, and upon the right shoulder.
8.27: So hee put all in Aarons handes, and in his sonnes handes, and shook it to and from before the Lord.
8.28: After, Moses took the out of their hands, and burnt them upon the altar for a burnt offring: for these were consecrations for a sweet sauour which were made by fire unto the Lord.
8.29: Likewise Moses took the breast of the ram of consecrations, and shook it to and from before the Lord: for it was Moses portion, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
8.30: Also Moses took of the anointing oyle, and of the blood which was upon the Altar, and sprinkled it upon Aaron, upon his garments, and upon his sonnes, and on his sonnes garments with him: so hee sanctified Aaron, his garments, and his sonnes, and his sonnes garments with him.
8.31: Afterward Moses said unto Aaron and his sonnes, Seethe the flesh at the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation, and there eat it with the bread that is in the basket of consecrations, as I commanded, saying, Aaron and his sonnes shall eat it,
8.32: But that which remaineth of the flesh and of the bread, shall ye burn with fire.
8.33: And ye shall not depart from the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation seven dayes, until the dayes of your consecrations bee at an end: for seven dayes, said the Lord, shall hee consecrate you,
8.34: As hee hath done this day: so the Lord hath commanded to doe, to make an atonement for you.
8.35: Therefore shall yee abide at the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation day and night, seven dayes, and shall keep the watch of the Lord, that ye dye not: for so I am commanded.
8.36: So Aaron and his sonnes did all thinges which the Lord had commanded by the hand of Moses.

9.1: And in the eight day Moses called Aaron and his sonnes, and the Elders of Israel:
9.2: Then hee sayde unto Aaron, Take thee a yong calf for a sinne offring, and a ram for a burnt offring, both without blemish, and bring them before the Lord.
9.3: And unto the children of Israel thou shalt speak, saying, Take yee an hee goat for a sinne offring, and a calf, and a lamb, both of a yeere old, without blemish for a burnt offring:
9.4: Also a bullock, and a ramme for peace offringes, to offer before the Lord, and a meat offring mingled with oyle: for to day the Lord will appear unto you.
9.5: Then they brought that which Moses commanded before the Tabernacle of the Congregation, and all the assembly drew neere and stood before the Lord.
9.6: (For Moses had sayde, This is the thing, which the Lord commanded that ye should do, and the glory of the Lord shall appear unto you)
9.7: Then Moses sayd unto Aaron, Draw neere to the Altar, and offer thy sinne offering, and thy burnt offring, and make an atonement for thee and for the people: offer also the offring of the people, and make an atonement for them, as the Lord hath commanded.
9.8: Aaron therefore went unto the Altar, and killed the calf of the sinne offring, which was for himself.
9.9: And the sonnes of Aaron brought ye blood unto him, and he dipt his finger in the blood, and put it upon the hornes of the Altar, and powred the rest of the blood at the foot of the Altar.
9.10: But the fat and the kidneis and the kall of the liver of the sinne offring, he burnt upon the Altar, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
9.11: The flesh also and the hide hee burnt with fire without the host.
9.12: After, he slew the burnt offering, and Aarons sonnes brought unto him the blood, which he sprinckled round about upon the Altar.
9.13: Also they brought the burnt offring unto him with the pieces thereof, and the head, and he burnt them upon the Altar.
9.14: Likewise he did wash the inwardes and the legs, and burnt them upon the burnt offring on the Altar.
9.15: Then he offred the peoples offring, and took a goat, which was the sinne offring for the people, and slew it: and offred it for sinne, as the first:
9.16: So he offred the burnt offring, and prepared it, according to the maner.
9.17: He presented also the meat offring, and filled his hand thereof, and beside the burnt sacrifice of the morning he burnt this upon the Altar.
9.18: He slew also the bullock, and the ram for the peace offrings, that was for the people, and Arons sonnes brought unto him the blood, which he sprinkled upon the Altar round about,
9.19: With the fat of the bullock, and of the ram, the rump, and that which covereth the inwards and the kidneis, and the kall of the liver.
9.20: So they layed the fat upon the breasts, and he burnt the fat upon the Altar.
9.21: But the breastes and the right shoulder Aaron shook to and from before the Lord, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
9.22: So Aaron lift up his hand toward the people, and blessed them, and came down from offring of the sinne offring, and the burnt offring, and the peace offrings.
9.23: After, Moses and Aaron went into the Tabernacle of the Congregation, and came out, and blessed the people, and the glorie of the Lord appeared to all the people.
9.24: And there came a fire out from the Lord and consumed upon the Altar the burnt offring and the fatte: which when all the people saw, they gave thankes, and fell on their faces.

10.1: But Nadab and Abihu, the sonnes of Aaron, took either of them his censor, and put fire therein, and put incense thereupon, and offred strange fire before the Lord, which hee had not commanded them.
10.2: Therefore a fire went out from the Lord, and deuoured them: so they dyed before the Lord.
10.3: Then Moses sayde unto Aaron, This is it that the Lord spake, saying, I will bee sanctified in the that come neere me, and before all the people I will be glorified: but Aaron held his peace.
10.4: And Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan the sonnes of Uzziel, the uncle of Aaron, and said unto them, Come neere, cary your brethre from before the Sanctuarie out of the host.
10.5: Then they went, and caried them in their coates out of the host, as Moses had comaunded.
10.6: After, Moses said unto Aaron and unto Eleazar and Ithamar his sonnes, Vncouer not your heads, neither rent your clothes, least ye dye, and least wrath come upon all ye people: but let your brethren, all the house of Israel bewayle the burning which the Lord hath kindled.
10.7: And go not yee out from the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation, least ye dye: for the anointing oyle of the Lord is upon you: and they did according to Moses commandement.
10.8: And the Lord spake unto Aaron, saying,
10.9: Thou shalt not drink wine nor strong drink, thou, nor thy sonnes with thee, when yee come into the Tabernacle of the Congregation, lest ye die: this is an ordinance for ever throughout your generations,
10.10: That ye may put difference between the holy and the unholy, and between the clean and the vncleane,
10.11: And that ye may teach the children of Israel all the statutes which the Lord hath commanded them by the hand of Moses.
10.12: Then Moses said unto Aaron and unto Eleazar and to Ithamar his sonnes that were left, Take the meat offring that remaineth of the offrings of the Lord, made by fire, and eat it without leaven beside ye altar: for it is most holy:
10.13: And ye shall eat it in the holy place, because it is thy duetie and thy sonnes duety of the offringes of the Lord made by fire: for so I am commanded.
10.14: Also the shaken breast and the heave shoulder shall yee eat in a clean place: thou, and thy sonnes, and thy daughters with thee: for they are given as thy duetie and thy sonnes duety, of the peace offringes of the children of Israel.
10.15: The heave shoulder, and the shaken breast shall they bring with the offringes made by fire of the fat, to shake it to and from before the Lord, and it shalbe thine and thy sonnes with thee by a law for ever, as the Lord hath commanded.
10.16: And Moses sought the goat that was offred for sinne, and lo, it was burnt: therefore he was angrie with Eleazar and Ithamar the sonnes of Aaron, which were left alive, saying,
10.17: Wherfore have ye not eaten the sinne offring in the holy place, seeing it is most Holie? and God hath given it you, to bear the iniquitie of the Congregation, to make an atonement for them before the Lord.
10.18: Behold, the blood of it was not brought within the holy place: ye should have eaten it in the holy place, as I commanded.
10.19: And Aaron said unto Moses, Behold, this day have they offred their sinne offring, and their burnt offring before the Lord, and such things as thou knowest are come unto mee: If I had eaten the sinne offring to day, should it have been accepted in the sight of the Lord?
10.20: So when Moses heard it, he was content.

11.1: After, the Lord spake unto Moses and to Aaron, saying unto them,
11.2: Speak unto the children of Israel, and say, These are the beastes which yee shall eat, among all the beasts that are on the earth.
11.3: Whatsoever parteth the hoof, and is cloven footed, and cheweth the cudde, among the beastes, that shall ye eat.
11.4: But of them that chew the cud, or deuide the hoof onely, of them yee shall not eat: as the camel, because he cheweth the cud, and deuideth not ye hoof, he shall be vncleane unto you.
11.5: Likewise the conie, because he cheweth the cud and deuideth not the hoof, he shall bee vncleane to you.
11.6: Also the hare, because he cheweth the cud, and deuideth not the hoof, he shalbe vncleane to you.
11.7: And the swine, because he parteth ye hoof and is cloven footed, but cheweth not the cud, he shalbe vncleane to you.
11.8: Of their flesh shall yee not eat, and their carkeise shall yee not touch: for they shall bee vncleane to you.
11.9: These shall ye eat, of all that are in the waters: whatsoever hath finnes and skales in ye waters, in the seas, or in the rivers, them shall ye eat.
11.10: But all that have not finnes nor skales in the seas, or in the rivers, of all that moveth in the waters, and of al living things that are in the waters, they shalbe an abomination unto you.
11.11: They, I say, shalbe an abomination to you: ye shall not eat of their flesh, but shall abhorre their carkeis.
11.12: Whatsoever hath not fins nor skales in the waters, that shalbe abomination unto you.
11.13: These shall ye have also in abomination among the foules, they shall not be eaten: for they are an abomination, the eagle, and the goshauke, and the osprey:
11.14: Also the vultur, and the kite after his kind,
11.15: And all ravens after their kind:
11.16: The ostrich also, and the night crow, and the seameaw, and the hauke after his kind:
11.17: The litle owl also, and the connorant, and the great owl.
11.18: Also the redshanke and the pelican, and the swanne:
11.19: The stork also, the heron after his kind, and the lapwing, and the back:
11.20: Also every fowl that creepeth and goeth upon all four, such shalbe an abomination unto you.
11.21: Yet these shall ye eat: of every fowl that creepeth, and goeth upon all four which have their feet and legs all of one to leap withal upon the earth,
11.22: Of them ye shall eat these, the grashopper after his kind, and the solean after his kind, the hargol after his kind, and the hagab after his kind.
11.23: But al other foules that creep and have four feet, they shalbe abomination unto you.
11.24: For by such ye shalbe polluted: whosoever toucheth their carkeis, shalbe vncleane unto the evening.
11.25: Whosoever also beareth of their carkeis, shall wash his clothes, and be vncleane until even.
11.26: Every beast that hath clawes deuided, and is not cloven footed, nor cheweth the cud, such shalbe vncleane unto you: every one that toucheth them, shalbe vncleane.
11.27: And whatsoever goeth upon his pawes among all maner beastes that goeth on all four, such shalbe vncleane unto you: who so doth touch their carkeis shalbe vncleane until the even.
11.28: And he that beareth their carkeis, shall wash his clothes, and be vncleane until the even: for such shalbe vncleane unto you.
11.29: Also these shalbe vncleane to you amog the things that creep and move upon the earth, the weasel, and the mouse, and the frog, after his kind:
11.30: Also the rat, and the lizard, and the chameleon, and the stellio, and the mole.
11.31: These shall be vncleane to you among all that creep: whosoever doeth touch them when they be dead, shalbe vncleane until the even.
11.32: Also whatsoever any of the dead carkeises of them doth fall upon, shalbe vncleane, whether it be vessel of wood, or rayment, or skinne, or sack: whatsoever vessel it be that is occupied, it shalbe put in the water as vncleane until the even, and so be purified.
11.33: But every earthen vessel, whereinto any of them falleth, whatsoever is within it shalbe vncleane, and ye shall break it.
11.34: Al meat also that shalbe eaten, if any such water come upon it, shalbe vncleane: and all drink that shalbe drunk in al such vessels shalbe vncleane.
11.35: And every thing that their carkeis fall upon, shalbe vncleane: the fornais or the pot shalbe broken: for they are vncleane, and shalbe vncleane unto you.
11.36: Yet the fountaines and welles where there is plentie of water shalbe clean: but that which toucheth their carkeises shalbe vncleane.
11.37: And if there fal of their dead carkeis upon any seed, which useth to be sow, it shalbe clean.
11.38: But if any water be powred upon ye seed, and there fal of their dead carkeis thereon, it shall be vncleane unto you.
11.39: If also any beast, whereof ye may eat, die, he that toucheth the carkeis thereof shall be vncleane until the even.
11.40: And he that eateth of the carkeis of it, shall wash his clothes and be vncleane until the even: he also that beareth the carkeis of it, shall wash his clothes, and be vncleane until the even.
11.41: Every creeping thing therefore that creepeth upon the earth shalbe an abomination, and not be eaten.
11.42: Whatsoever goeth upon the breast, and whatsoever goeth upon al four, or that hath many feet among all creeping thinges that creep upon the earth, ye shall not eat of them, for they shalbe abomination.
11.43: Ye shall not pollute your selves with any thing that creepeth, neither make your selves vncleane with them, neither defile your selves thereby: ye shall not, I say, be defiled by them,
11.44: For I am the Lord your God: be sanctified therefore, and be holy, for I am holy, and defile not your selves with any creeping thing, that creepeth upon the earth.
11.45: For I am the Lord that brought you out of the land of Egypt, to be your God, and that you should be holy, for I am holy.
11.46: This is the law of beasts, and of foules, and of every living thing that moveth in the waters, and of every thing that creepeth upon the earth:
11.47: That there may be a difference between the vncleane and clean, and between the beast that may be eaten, and the beast that ought not to be eaten.

12.1: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
12.2: Speak unto the children of Israel, and say, When a woman hath brought forth seed, and borne a manchilde, she shalbe vncleane seven dayes, like as she is vncleane when she is put apart for her disease.
12.3: (And in the eight day, the foreskin of the childes flesh shalbe circumcised)
12.4: And she shall continue in the blood of her purifying three and thirtie dayes: she shall touch no halowed thing, nor come into the Sanctuarie, until the time of her purifying be out.
12.5: But if she bear a mayde child, then she shalbe vncleane two weekes, as when she hath her disease: and she shall continue in the blood of her purifying three score and six dayes.
12.6: Now when the dayes of her purifying are out, (whether it be for a sonne or for a daughter) she shall bring to the Priest a lamb of one yeere old for a burnt offering, and a yong pigeon or a turtle dove for a sinne offring, unto the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation,
12.7: Who shall offer it before the Lord, and make an atonement for her: so she shalbe purged of the issue of her blood this is the law for her that hath borne a male or female.
12.8: But if she bee not able to bring a lamb, she shall bring two turtles, or two yong pigeons: the one for a burnt offring, and the other for a sinne offring: and the Priest shall make an atonement for her: so she shall be clean.

13.1: Moreover the Lord spake unto Moses, and to Aaron, saying,
13.2: The man that shall have in the skin of his flesh a swelling or a skab, or a white spot, so that in the skinne of his flesh it be like the plague of leprosie, then he shalbe brought unto Aaron the Priest, or unto one of his sonnes the Priestes,
13.3: And the Priest shall look on the sore in the skinne of his flesh: if the hear in the sore be turned into white, and the sore seem to be lower then the skinne of his flesh, it is a plague of leprosie. therefore the Priest shall look on him, and pronounce him vncleane:
13.4: But if the white spot be in the skinne of his flesh, and seem not to bee lower then the skin, nor the hear thereof be turned unto white, then the Priest shall shut up him that hath the plague, seven dayes.
13.5: After, the Priest shall look upon him the seventh day: and if the plague seem to him to abide still, and the plague grow not in the skin, the Priest shall shut him up yet seven dayes more.
13.6: Then the Priest shall look on him again the seventh day, and if the plague be dark, and the sore grow not in the skinne, then the Priest shall pronounce him clean, for it is a skab: therefore he shall wash his clothes and be clean.
13.7: But if the skab grow more in the skinne, after that he is seen of ye Priest for to be purged, he shall be seen of the Priest yet again.
13.8: Then the Priest shall consider, and if the skab grow in the skin, then the Priest shall pronounce him vncleane: for it is leprosie.
13.9: When the plague of leprosie is in a man, he shalbe brought unto the Priest,
13.10: And the Priest shall see him: and if the swelling be white in ye skin, and have made ye hear white, and there be raw flesh in the swelling,
13.11: It is an old leprosie in the skin of his flesh: and the Priest shall pronounce him vncleane, and shall not shut him up, for he is vncleane.
13.12: Also if the leprosie break out in the skin, and the leprosie cover all the skin of the plague, from his head even to his feet, wheresoever the Priest looketh,
13.13: Then the Priest shall consider: and if the leprosie cover all his flesh, he shall pronounce the plague to bee clean, because it is all turned into whitenesse: so he shalbe clean.
13.14: But if there be raw flesh on him when he is seen, he shalbe vncleane.
13.15: For the Priest shall see the raw flesh, and declare him to be vncleane: for the raw flesh is vncleane, therefore it is the leprosie.
13.16: Or if the raw flesh change and be turned into white, then he shall come to the Priest,
13.17: And the Priest shall behold him and if the sore be changed into white, then the Priest shall pronounce the plague clean, for it is clean.
13.18: The flesh also in whose skin there is a bile and is healed,
13.19: And in ye place of the bile there be a white swelling, or a white spot somewhat reddish, it shall be seen of the Priest.
13.20: And when the Priest seeth it, if it appear lower then the skinne, and the hear thereof bee changed into white, ye Priest then shall pronounce him vncleane: for it is a plague of leprosie, broken out in the bile.
13.21: But if the Priest look on it, and there be no white heares therein, and if it bee not lower then the skin, but be darker, then the Priest shall shut him up seven dayes.
13.22: And if it spred abroad in the flesh, ye Priest shall pronounce him vncleane, for it is a sore.
13.23: But if the spot continue in his place, and grow not, it is a burning bile: therefore the Priest shall declare him to be clean.
13.24: If there be any flesh, in whose skin there is an hot burning, and the quick flesh of ye burning have a white spot, somewhat reddish or pale,
13.25: Then the Priest shall look upon it: and if the hear in that spot be changed into white, and it appear lower then the skin, it is a leprosie broken out in the burning therefore the Priest shall pronounce him vncleane: for it is the plague of leprosie.
13.26: But if the Priest look on it, and there be no white hear in the spot, and be no lower then the other skinne, but be darker, then the Priest shall shut him up seven dayes.
13.27: After, the Priest shall look on him the seventh day: if it be growen abroad in the skinne, then the Priest shall pronounce him vncleane: for it is the plague of leprosie.
13.28: And if the spot abide in his place, not growing in the skin, but is dark, it is a rising of the burning: the Priest shall therefore declare him clean, for it is the drying up of the burning.
13.29: If also a man or woman hath a sore on the head or in the beard,
13.30: Then the Priest shall see his sore: and if it appear lower then the skin, and there be in it a small yellow hair, then the Priest shall pronouce him vncleane: for it is a black spot, and leprosie of the head or of the beard.
13.31: And if the Priest look on the sore of the black spotte, and if it seem not lower then the skinne, nor have any black hear in it, then the Priest shall shut up him, that hath the sore of the black spot, seven dayes.
13.32: After, in the seventh day the Priest shall look on the sore: and if the black spot grow not, and there be in it no yelowe hear, and the black spot seem not lower then the skinne,
13.33: Then he shalbe shaven, but the place of the black spot shall he not shave: but the Priest shall shut up him, that hath the black spot, seven dayes more.
13.34: And the seventh day the Priest shall look on the black spot: and if the black spot grow not in the skinne, nor seem lower then the other skinne, then the Priest shall clense him, and hee shall wash his clothes, and be clean.
13.35: But if the black spot grow abroad in the flesh after his clensing,
13.36: Then the Priest shall look on it: and if the black spot grow in the skin, the Priest shall not seek for the yelowe hear: for he is vncleane.
13.37: But if ye black spot seem to him to abide, and that black hear grow therein, the black spot is healed, he is clean, and the Priest shall declare him to be clean.
13.38: Furthermore if there bee many white spots in the skin of the flesh of man or woman,
13.39: Then the Priest shall consider: and if the spots in the skin of their flesh be somewhat dark and white withal, it is but a white spot broken out in the skin: therefore he is clean.
13.40: And the man whose hear is fallen off his head, and is bald, is clean.
13.41: And if his head lose the hear on the forepart, and be bald before, he is clean.
13.42: But if there be in the bald head, or in the bald forehead a white reddish sore, it is a leprosie springing in his bald head, or in his bald forehead.
13.43: Therefore the Priest shall look upon it, and if the rising of the sore bee white reddish in his bald head, or in his bald forehead, appearing like leprosie in the skin of the flesh,
13.44: He is a leper and vncleane: therefore the Priest shall pronounce him altogether vncleane: for the sore is in his head.
13.45: The leper also in whom the plague is, shall have his clothes rent, and his head bare, and shall put a covering upon his lips, and shall cry, I am vncleane, I am vncleane.
13.46: As long as the disease shall be upon him, he shalbe polluted, for he is vncleane: he shall dwell alone, without the camp shall his habitation be.
13.47: Also the garment that the plague of leprosie is in, whether it be a wollen garment or a linen garment,
13.48: Whether it bee in the warp or in ye woof of linen or of wollen, either in a skin, or in any thing made of skin,
13.49: And if the sore be green or somewhat reddish in the garment or in ye skin, or in the warp, or in the woof, or in any thing that is made of skin, it is a plague of leprosie and shalbe shewed unto the Priest.
13.50: Then the Priest shall see the plague, and shut up it that hath the plague, seven dayes,
13.51: And shall look on the plague the seventh day: if the plague grow in the garment or in the warp, or in the woof, or in the skinne, or in any thing that is made of skin, that plague is a fretting leprosie and vncleane.
13.52: And hee shall burn the garment, or the warp, or the woof, whether it bee wollen or linen, or any thing that is made of skin, wherein the plague is: for it is a freating leprosie, therefore it shalbe burnt in the fire.
13.53: If the Priest yet see that the plague grow not in the garment, or in the woof, or in whatsoever thing of skin it be,
13.54: Then the Priest shall commaund them to wash the thing wherein the plague is, and he shall shut it up seven dayes more.
13.55: Again ye Priest shall look on the plague, after it is washed: and if the plague have not changed his colour, though the plague have spred no further, it is vncleane: thou shalt burn it in the fire, for it is a fret inward, whether the spot bee in the bare place of the whole, or in part thereof.
13.56: And if the Priest see that the plague bee darker, after that it is washed, he shall cut it out of the garment, or out of the skin, or out of the warp, or out of the woof.
13.57: And if it appear stil in ye garment or in the warp, or in the woof, or in any thing made of skin, it is a spreading leprie: thou shalt burn the thing wherein the plague is, in the fire.
13.58: If thou hast washed ye garment or ye warp, or ye woof, or whatsouer thing of skin it be, if the plague be departed therefrom, then shall it be washed the second time, and be clean.
13.59: This is the law of the plague of leprosie in a garment of wollen or linen, or in the warp, or in the woof, or in any thing of skin, to make it clean or vncleane.

14.1: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
14.2: This is the law of the leper in the day of his clensing: that is, he shall be brought unto the Priest,
14.3: And the Priest shall go out of the camp, and the Priest shall consider him: and if the plague of leprosie be healed in the leper,
14.4: Then shall the Priest commaund to take for him that is clensed, two sparrowes alive and clean, and cedar wood and a skarlet lace, and hyssop.
14.5: And the Priest shall commaund to kill one of the birdes over pure water in an earthen vessell.
14.6: After, he shall take the live sparowe with the cedar wood, and the skarlet lace, and the hyssop, and shall dip them and the living sparowe in the blood of the sparowe slain, over the pure water,
14.7: And hee shall sprinkle upon him, that must be clensed of his leprosie, seven times, and clense him, and shall let goe the live sparowe into the broad field.
14.8: Then he that shall be clensed, shall wash his clothes, and shave off all his hear, and wash himself in water, so he shalbe clean: after that shall he come into the host, but shall tary without his tent seven dayes.
14.9: So in the seventh day hee shall shave off all his hear, both his head, and his beard, and his eye browes: even all his hear shall he shave, and shall wash his clothes and shall wash his flesh in water: so he shalbe clean.
14.10: Then in the eight day he shall take two hee lambes without blemish, and an ewe lamb of a yere old without blemish, and three tenth deales of fine flower for a meat offering, mingled with oyle, and a pint of oyle.
14.11: And the Priest that maketh him clean shall bring the man which is to bee made clean, and those things, before the Lord, at the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation.
14.12: Then the Priest shall take one lamb, and offer him for a trespass offering, and the pint of oyle, and shake the to and from before the Lord.
14.13: And hee shall kill the lamb in the place where the sinne offring and the burnt offring are slain, even in the holy place: for as the sinne offring is the Priests, so is the trespass offring: for it is most holy.
14.14: So the Priest shall take of the blood of the trespass offring, and put it upon the lappe of the right ear of him that shalbe clensed, and upon the thumb of his right hand, and upon the great toe of his right foot.
14.15: The Priest shall also take of ye pint of oyle, and powre it into the palm of his left hand,
14.16: And the Priest shall dip his right finger in the oyle that is in his left hand, and sprinkle of the oyle with his finger seven times before the Lord.
14.17: And of the rest of the oyle that is in his hand, shall the Priest put upon the lap of the right ear of him that is to bee clensed, and upon the thumb of his right hand, and upon the great toe of his right foot, where the blood of the trespass offring was put.
14.18: But the remnant of the oyle that is in the Priests hand, he shall powre upon the head of him that is to be clensed: so the Priest shall make an atonement for him before the Lord.
14.19: And the Priest shall offer the sinne offring and make an atonement for him that is to bee clensed of his vncleannesse: then after shall he kill the burnt offring.
14.20: So the Priest shall offer ye burnt offring and the meat offring upon ye altar and the Priest shall make an atonement for him: so he shalbe clean.
14.21: But if he be poor, and not able, then he shall bring one lamb for a trespass offring to be shaken, for his reconciliation, and a tenth deal of fine flower mingled with oyle, for a meat offring, with a pinte of oyle.
14.22: Also two turtle doves, or two yong pigeons, as he is able, whereof the one shalbe a sinne offering, and the other a burnt offring,
14.23: And he shall bring them the eight day for his clensing unto the Priest at the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation before ye Lord.
14.24: The the Priest shall take the lamb of the trespass offring, and the pint of oyle, and the Priest shall shake them to and from before the Lord.
14.25: And he shall kill the lamb of the trespass offering, and the Priest shall take of the blood of the trespass offring, and put it upon the lap of his right ear that is to be clensed, and upon ye thumb of his right hand, and upon the great toe of his right foot.
14.26: Also the Priest shall powre of the oyle into the palm of his own left hand.
14.27: So ye Priest shall with his right finger sprinkle of the oyle that is in his left hand, seven times before the Lord.
14.28: Then the Priest shall put of the oyle that is in his hand, upon the lap of the right ear of him that is to bee clensed, and upon the thumb of his right hand, and upon the great toe of his right foot: upon the place of the blood of the trespass offring.
14.29: But ye rest of the oyle that is in the Priests hand, he shall put upon the head of him that is to be clensed, to make an atonement for him before the Lord.
14.30: Also hee shall present one of the turtle doves, or of the yong pigeons, as he is able:
14.31: Such, I say, as he is able, the one for a sinne offring, and the other for a burnt offring with the meat offring: so the Priest shall make an atonement for him that is to bee clensed before the Lord.
14.32: This is the law of him which hath the plague of leprosie, who is not able in his clensing to offer the whole.
14.33: The Lord also spake unto Moses and to Aaron, saying,
14.34: When ye be come unto the land of Canaan which I give you in possession, if I send the plague of leprosie in an house of the land of your possession,
14.35: Then he that oweth the house, shall come and tell the Priest, saying, Me think there is like a plague of leprosie in the house.
14.36: Then the Priest shall command them to emptie the house before the Priest goe into it to see the plague, that all that is in the house be not made vncleane, and then shall the Priest goe in to see the house,
14.37: And hee shall mark the plague: and if the plague be in the walles of the house, and that there be deep spots, greenish or reddish, which seem to be lower then the wall,
14.38: Then the Priest shall goe out of the house to the door of the house, and shall cause to shut up the house seven dayes.
14.39: So the Priest shall come again ye seventh day: and if he see that the plague bee increased in the walles of the house,
14.40: Then the Priest shall command them to take away the stones wherein the plague is, and they shall cast them into a fowl place without the citie.
14.41: Also hee shall cause to scrape the house within round about, and powre the dust, that they have pared off, without the citie in an vncleane place.
14.42: And they shall take other stones, and put them in the places of those stones, and shall take other mortar, to plaister the house with.
14.43: But if the plague come again and break out in the house, after that he hath taken away ye stones, and after that hee hath scraped and playstered the house,
14.44: Then the Priest shall come and see: and if the plague grow in the house, it is a freating leprosie in the house: it is therefore vncleane.
14.45: And hee shall break down the house, with the stones of it, and the timber thereof, and all the mortar of the house, and hee shall carie them out of the citie unto an vncleane place.
14.46: Moreover he that goeth into the house all the while that it is shut up, hee shall bee vncleane until the even.
14.47: Hee also that sleepeth in the house shall wash his clothes: he likewise that eateth in the house, shall wash his clothes.
14.48: But if the Priest shall come and see, that the plague hath spread no further in the house, after the house be plaistered, the Priest shall pronounce that house clean, for the plague is healed.
14.49: Then shall he take to purifie the house, two sparrowes, and cedar wood, and skarlet lace, and hyssop.
14.50: And hee shall kill one sparowe over pure water in an earthen vessell,
14.51: And shall take the cedar wood, and the hyssop, and the skarlet lace with the live Sparrow, and dip them in the blood of the slayne Sparrow, and in the pure water, and sprinkle the house seven times:
14.52: So shall hee clense the house with ye blood of the sparowe, and with the pure water, and with the live sparowe, and with the cedar wood, and with the hyssop, and with the skarlet lace.
14.53: Afterward he shall let go the live sparowe out of the town into the broad fieldes: so shall he make atonement for the house, and it shall be clean.
14.54: This is the law for every plague of leprosie and black spot,
14.55: And of the leprosie of the garment, and of the house,
14.56: And of the swelling, and of the skab, and of the white spot.
14.57: This is the law of the leprosie to teach when a thing is vncleane, and when it is clean.

15.1: Moreover the Lord spake unto Moses, and to Aaron, saying,
15.2: Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, Whosoever hath an issue from his flesh, is vncleane, because of his issue.
15.3: And this shalbe his vncleannes in his issue: when his flesh auoydeth his issue, or if his flesh be stopped from his issue, this is his vncleannes.
15.4: Every bed whereon he lyeth that hath the issue, shall be vncleane, and every thing whereon he sitteth, shalbe vncleane.
15.5: Whosoever also toucheth his bed, shall wash his clothes, and wash himself in water, and shall be vncleane until the even.
15.6: And he that sitteth on any thing, whereon he sat that hath the issue, shall wash his clothes, and wash himself in water, and shalbe vncleane until the even.
15.7: Also he that toucheth the flesh of him that hath the issue, shall wash his clothes, and wash himself in water, and shalbe vncleane until the even.
15.8: If he also, that hath the issue, spit upon him that is clean, he shall wash his clothes, and wash himself in water, and shalbe vncleane until the even.
15.9: And what saddle soever he rideth upon, that hath the issue, shalbe vncleane,
15.10: And whosoever toucheth any thing that was under him, shall be vncleane unto the even: and he that beareth those things, shall wash his clothes, and wash himself in water, and shall be vncleane until the even.
15.11: Likewise whomesoeuer hee toucheth that hath the issue (and hath not washed his handes in water) shall wash his clothes and wash himself in water, and shalbe vncleane until the even.
15.12: And the vessel of earth that he toucheth, which hath the issue, shalbe broken: and every vessel of wood shalbe rinsed in water.
15.13: But if he that hath an issue, be cleansed of his issue, then shall he count him seven dayes for his cleansing, and wash his clothes, and wash his flesh in pure water: so shall he be clean.
15.14: Then the eight day he shall take unto him two Turtle doves or two yong pigeons, and come before the Lord at the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation, and shall give them unto the Priest.
15.15: And the Priest shall make of the one of them a sinne offring, and of the other a burnt offering: so the Priest shall make an atonement for him before the Lord, for his issue.
15.16: Also if any mans issue of seed depart from him, he shall wash all his flesh in water, and be vncleane until the even.
15.17: And every garment, and every skinne whereupon shalbe issue of seed, shall be even washed with water, and be vncleane unto the even.
15.18: If he that hath an issue of seed, do lie with a woman, they shall both wash themselves with water, and be vncleane until the even.
15.19: Also when a woman shall have an issue, and her issue in her flesh shalbe blood, she shalbe put apart seven dayes: and whosoever toucheth her, shalbe vncleane unto the even.
15.20: And whatsoever she lieth upon in her separation, shalbe vncleane, and every thing that she sitteth upon, shalbe vncleane.
15.21: Whosoever also toucheth her bedde, shall wash his clothes, and wash himself with water, and shalbe vncleane unto the even.
15.22: And whosoever toucheth any thing that she sat upon, shall wash his clothes, and wash him self in water, and shalbe vncleane unto the even:
15.23: So that whether he touch her bed, or any thing whereon she hath sit, he shalbe vncleane unto the even.
15.24: And if a man lye with her, and the flowers of her separation touch him, he shalbe vncleane seven dayes, and all the whole bed whereon he lieth, shalbe vncleane.
15.25: Also when a womans issue of blood runneth long time besides the time of her floures, or when she hath an issue, longer then her floures, all the dayes of the issue of her vncleannesse she shalbe vncleane, as in the time of her floures.
15.26: Every bed whereon she lyeth (as long as her issue lasteth) shalbe to her as her bed of her separation: and whatsoever she sitteth upon, shalbe vncleane, as her vncleannes whe she is put apart.
15.27: And whosoever toucheth these things, shall be vncleane, and shall wash his clothes, and wash him self in water, and shalbe vncleane unto the even.
15.28: But if she be clensed of her issue, then she shall count her seven dayes, and after, she shall be clean.
15.29: And in the eight day she shall take unto her two Turtles or two yong pigeons, and bring them unto the Priest at the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation.
15.30: And the Priest shall make of ye one a sinne offring, and of the other a burnt offring, and the Priest shall make an atonement for her before the Lord, for the issue of her vncleannes.
15.31: Thus shall yee separate the children of Israel from their vncleannes, that they dye not in their vncleannesse, if they defile my Tabernacle that is among them.
15.32: This is the law of him that hath an issue, and of him from whom goeth an issue of seed whereby he is defiled:
15.33: Also of her that is sick of her floures, and of him that hath a running issue, whether it bee man or woman, and of him that lyeth with her which is vncleane.

16.1: Furthermore the Lord spake unto Moses, after the death of the two sonnes of Aaron, whe they came to offer before the Lord, and dyed:
16.2: And the Lord sayd unto Moses, Speak unto Aaron thy brother, that he come not at all times into the Holy place within the vayle, before the Merciseate, which is upon the Ark, that he dye not: for I wil appear in the cloud upon the Merciseate.
16.3: After this sort shall Aaron come into the Holy place: even with a yong bullock for a sinne offring, and a ramme for a burnt offring.
16.4: He shall put on the holy linen coat, and shall have linen breeches upon his flesh, and shall be girded with a linen girdle, and shall cover his head with a linen miter: these are the holy garments: therefore shall hee wash his flesh in water, when he doeth put them on.
16.5: And hee shall take of the Congregation of the children of Israel, two hee goates for a sinne offring, and a ramme for a burnt offring.
16.6: Then Aaron shall offer the bullock for his sinne offring, and make an atonement for himself, and for his house.
16.7: And he shall take the two hee goates, and present them before the Lord at the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation.
16.8: Then Aaron shall cast lots over the two hee goates: one lot for the Lord, and the other for the Scape goat.
16.9: And Aaron shall offer the goat, upon which the Lords lot shall fal, and make him a sinne offring.
16.10: But the goat, on which the lot shall fall to be the Scape goat, shalbe presented alive before the Lord, to make reconciliation by him, and to let him go (as a Scape goat) into the wildernes.
16.11: Thus Aaron shall offer the bullock for his sinne offring, and make a reconciliation for himself, and for his house, and shall kill the bullock for his sinne offring.
16.12: And he shall take a censer full of burning coles from off the altar before the Lord, and his handful of sweet incense beaten small, and bring it within the vayle,
16.13: And shall put the incense upon the fire before the Lord, that the cloud of the incense may cover the Merciseat that is upon the Testimonie: so he shall not dye.
16.14: And hee shall take of the blood of the bullock, and sprinkle it with his finger upon the Merciseat Eastward: and before the Merciseate shall he sprinkle of the blood with his finger seven times.
16.15: Then shall he kill the goat that is the peoples sinne offring, and bring his blood within the vail, and doe with that blood, as he did with the blood of the bullock, and sprinckle it upon the Merciseate, and before the Merciseate.
16.16: So he shall purge the Holy place from the vncleannes of the children of Israel, and from their trespasses of all their sinnes: so shall he do also for the Tabernacle of the Cogregation placed with them, in the middes of their vncleannesse.
16.17: And there shalbe no man in the Tabernacle of the Congregation, when he goeth in to make an atonement in the Holy place, until hee come out, and have made an atonement for himself, and for his housholde, and for all the Congregation of Israel.
16.18: After, he shall goe out unto the altar that is before the Lord and make a reconciliation upon it, and shall take of the blood of the bullock, and of the blood of the goat, and put it upon the hornes of the Altar round about:
16.19: So shall hee sprinkle of the blood upon it with his finger seven times, and clense it, and halowe it from the vncleannes of the children of Israel.
16.20: When he hath made an end of purging the Holy place, and the Tabernacle of the Congregation, and the altar, then he shall bring the live goat:
16.21: And Aaron shall put both his handes upon the head of the live goat, and confess over him al the iniquities of the children of Israel, and all their trespasses, in all their sinnes, putting them upon the head of the goat, and shall send him away (by the hand of a man appointed) into the wildernes.
16.22: So the goat shall bear upon him all their iniquities into the land that is not inhabited, and he shall let the goat go into the wilderness.
16.23: After, Aaron shall come into the Tabernacle of the Congregation, and put off the linen clothes, which he put on when he went into the Holy place, and leave them there.
16.24: Hee shall wash also his flesh with water in the Holy place, and put on his own rayment, and come out, and make his burnt offring, and the burnt offring of the people, and make an atonement for himself, and for the people.
16.25: Also the fatte of the sinne offring shall he burn upon the altar.
16.26: And he that caried forth the goat, called the Scape goat, shall wash his clothes, and wash his flesh in water, and after that shall come into the host.
16.27: Also the bullock for the sinne offring, and the goat for the sinne offring (whose blood was brought to make a reconciliation in the Holy place) shall one carie out without the host to be burnt in the fire, with their skinnes, and with their flesh, and with their doung.
16.28: And hee that burneth them shall wash his clothes, and wash his flesh in water, and afterward come into the host.
16.29: So this shalbe an ordinance for ever unto you: the tenth day of the seventh moneth, yee shall humble your soules, and do no work at all, whether it be one of the same countrey or a strager that soiourneth among you.
16.30: For that day shall ye Priest make an atonement for you to clense you: ye shalbe clean from all your sinnes before the Lord.
16.31: This shall be a Sabbath of rest unto you, and ye shall humble your soules, by an ordinance for ever.
16.32: And the Priest whom he shall anoynt, and whom he shall cosecrate (to minister in his fathers stead) shall make the atonement, and shall put on the linen clothes and Holy vestments,
16.33: And shall purge the Holy Sanctuarie and the Tabernacle of the Congregation, and shall clense the altar, and make an atonement for the Priests and for all the people of the Congregation.
16.34: And this shalbe an everlasting ordinance unto you, to make an atonement for the children of Israel for all their sinnes once a yeere: and as the Lord commanded Moses, he did.

17.1: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
17.2: Speak unto Aaron, and to his sonnes, and to all the children of Israel, and say unto them, This is the thing which the Lord hath commanded, saying,
17.3: Whosoever he be of the house of Israel that killeth a bullock, or lamb, or goat in the host, or that killeth it out of the host,
17.4: And bringeth it not unto the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation to offer an offring unto the Lord before the Tabernacle of the Lord, blood shalbe imputed unto that man: he hath shed blood, wherefore that man shall be cut off from among his people.
17.5: Therefore the children of Israel shall bring their offrings, which they would offer abroad in the field, and present the unto ye Lord at the door of the Tabernacle of ye Congregation by ye Priest, and offer them for peace offrings unto the Lord.
17.6: Then the Priest shall sprinkle the blood upon the Altar of the Lord before the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation, and burn the fat for a sweet sauour unto the Lord.
17.7: And they shall no more offer their offerings unto devils, after whom they have gone a whoring: this shalbe an ordinance for ever unto them in their generations.
17.8: Also thou shalt say unto them, whosoever he be of the house of Israel, or of the strangers which soiourne among them, that offreth a burnt offring or sacrifice,
17.9: And bringeth it not unto ye door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation to offer it unto the Lord, even that man shall be cut off from his people.
17.10: Likewise whosoever he be of the house of Israel, or of the strangers that soiourne among them, that eateth any blood, I will even set my face against that person that eateth blood, and will cut him off from among his people.
17.11: For the life of the flesh is in the blood, and I have given it unto you to offer upon the altar, to make an atonement for your soules: for this blood shall make an atonement for the soul.
17.12: Therefore I said unto ye children of Israel, None of you shall eat blood: neither the stranger that soiourneth among you, shall eat blood.
17.13: Moreover whosoever he be of the children of Israel, or of the strangers that soiourne among the, which by hunting taketh any beast or fowl that may be eaten, he shall powre out the blood thereof, and cover it with dust:
17.14: For ye life of all flesh is his blood, it is ioyned with his life: therefore I sayd unto the children of Israel, Ye shall eat the blood of no flesh: for the life of al flesh is the blood thereof: whosoever eateth it, shalbe cut off.
