17.15: And every person that eateth it which dyeth alone, or that which is torn with beastes, whether it be one of the same countrey or a stranger, he shall both wash his clothes, and wash himself in water, and be vncleane unto the even: after he shalbe clean.
17.16: But if he wash them not, nor wash his flesh, then he shall bear his iniquitie.

18.1: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
18.2: Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, I am the Lord your God.
18.3: After ye doings of the land of Egypt, wherin ye dwelt, shall ye not doe: and after the maner of the land of Canaan, whither I will bring you, shall ye not do, neither walk in their ordinances,
18.4: But do after my iudgements, and keep mine ordinances, to walk therein: I am the Lord your God.
18.5: Ye shall keep therefore my statutes, and my iudgements, which if a man doe, he shall then live in them: I am the Lord.
18.6: None shall come neere to any of ye kinred of his flesh to vncouer her shame: I am the Lord.
18.7: Thou shalt not vncouer the shame of thy father, nor the shame of thy mother: for she is thy mother, thou shalt not discover her shame.
18.8: The shame of thy fathers wife shalt thou not discover: for it is thy fathers shame.
18.9: Thou shalt not discover the shame of thy sister the daughter of thy father, or the daughter of thy mother, whether she bee borne at home, or borne without: thou shalt not discover their shame.
18.10: The shame of thy sonnes daughter, or of thy daughters daughter, thou shalt not, I say, vncouer their shame: for it is thy shame.
18.11: The shame of thy fathers wives daughter, begotten of thy father (for she is thy sister) thou shalt not, I say, discover her shame.
18.12: Thou shalt not vncouer the shame of thy fathers sister: for she is thy fathers kinswoman.
18.13: Thou shalt not discover the shame of thy mothers sister: for she is thy mothers kinsewoman.
18.14: Thou shalt not vncouer the shame of thy fathers brother: that is, thou shalt not goe in to his wife, for she is thine aunt.
18.15: Thou shalt not discover the shame of thy daughter in law: for she is thy sonnes wife: therefore shalt thou not vncouer her shame.
18.16: Thou shalt not discover the shame of thy brothers wife. for it is thy brothers shame.
18.17: Thou shalt not discover the shame of the wife and of her daughter, neither shalt thou take her sonnes daughter, nor her daughters daughter, to vncouer her shame: for they are thy kinsfolkes, and it were wickedness.
18.18: Also thou shalt not take a wife with her sister, during her life, to vex her, in vncouering her shame upon her.
18.19: Thou shalt not also go unto a woman to vncouer her shame, as long as she is put apart for her disease.
18.20: Moreover, thou shalt not give thy self to thy neighbours wife by carnal copulation, to be defiled with her.
18.21: Also thou shalt not give thy children to offer them unto Molech, neither shalt thou defile the name of thy God: for I am the Lord.
18.22: Thou shalt not lie with ye male as one lieth with a woman: for it is abomination.
18.23: Thou shalt not also lie with any beast to bee defiled therewith, neither shall any woman stand before a beast, to lie down thereto: for it is abomination.
18.24: Yee shall not defile your selves in any of these things: for in al these the nations are defiled, which I will cast out before you:
18.25: And the land is defiled: therefore I wil visit the wickedness thereof upon it, and the land shall vomit out her inhabitants.
18.26: Ye shall keep therefore mine ordinances, and my iudgements, and commit none of these abominations, aswell hee that is of the same countrey, as the straunger that soiourneth among you.
18.27: (For all these abominations have the men of the land done, which were before you, and the land is defiled:
18.28: And shall not the land spue you out if ye defile it, as it spued out the people that were before you?)
18.29: For whosoever shall commit any of these abominations, the persons that doe so, shall bee cut off from among their people.
18.30: Therefore shall yee keep mine ordinances that ye do not any of the abominable customes, which have been done before you, and that yee defile not your selves therein: for I am the Lord your God.

19.1: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
19.2: Speak unto all the Congregation of the children of Israel, and say unto them, Ye shalbe holy, for I the Lord your God am holy.
19.3: Yee shall fear every man his mother and his father, and shall keep my Sabbaths: for I am the Lord your God.
19.4: Ye shall not turn unto idoles, nor make you molten gods: I am the Lord your God.
19.5: And when yee shall offer a peace offering unto the Lord, ye shall offer it freely.
19.6: It shall be eaten the day yee offer it, or on the morowe: and that which remaineth until the third day, shalbe burnt in the fire.
19.7: For if it be eaten the third day, it shall be vncleane, it shall not be accepted.
19.8: Therefore he that eateth it, shall bear his iniquitie, because he hath defiled the halowed thing of the Lord, and that person shalbe cut off from his people.
19.9: When yee reap the harvest of your land, ye shall not reap every corner of your field, neither shalt thou gather the glainings of thy harvest.
19.10: Thou shalt not gather the grapes of thy vineyard clean, neyther gather every grape of thy vineyard, but thou shalt leave them for the poor and for the straunger: I am the Lord your God.
19.11: Ye shall not steal, neither deal falsely, neither lie one to another.
19.12: Also yee shall not swear by my name falsely, neither shalt thou defile the name of thy God: I am the Lord.
19.13: Thou shalt not do thy neighbour wrong, neither rob him. The workemans hire shall not abide with thee until the morning.
19.14: Thou shalt not curse the deaf, neither put a stumbling blocke before the blind, but shalt fear thy God: I am the Lord.
19.15: Ye shall not doe vniustly in iudgement. Thou shalt not fauour the person of the poor, nor honour the person of the mightie, but thou shalt judge thy neighbour justly.
19.16: Thou shalt not walk about with tales among thy people. Thou shalt not stand against the blood of thy neighbour: I am the Lord.
19.17: Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart, but thou shalt plainely rebuke thy neighbour, and suffer him not to sinne.
19.18: Thou shalt not avenge, nor be mindful of wrong against ye childre of thy people, but shalt love thy neighbour as thy self: I am the Lord.
19.19: Yee shall keep mine ordinances. Thou shalt not let thy cattel gender with others of divers kindes. Thou shalt not sow thy field with mingled seed, neyther shall a garment of divers thinges, as of linen and wollen come upon thee.
19.20: Whosoever also lyeth and medleth with a woman that is a bond mayde, affianced to a husband, and not redeemed, nor freedom given her, she shalbe scourged, but they shall not die, because she is not made free.
19.21: And he shall bring for his trespass offring unto the Lord, at the door of the Tabernacle of the Congregation, a ramme for a trespass offering.
19.22: Then the Priest shall make an atonement for him with the ramme of the trespass offering before the Lord, concerning his sinne which he hath done, and pardon shalbe given him for his sinne which he hath committed.
19.23: Also when ye shall come into the land, and have planted every tree for meat, ye shall count the fruit thereof as uncircumcised: three yeere shall it be uncircumcised unto you, it shall not be eaten:
19.24: But in the fourth yere all the fruit thereof shalbe holy to the praise of the Lord.
19.25: And in the fifth yeere shall ye eat of the fruit of it that it may yeelde to you the encrease thereof: I am the Lord your God.
19.26: Ye shall not eat the flesh with the blood, ye shall not use witchcraft, nor observe times.
19.27: Ye shall not cut round the corners of your heades, neither shalt thou marre the tuftes of thy beard.
19.28: Ye shall not cut your flesh for the dead, nor make any print of a mark upon you: I am the Lord,
19.29: Thou shalt not make thy daughter common, to cause her to be a whore, least the land also fall to whoredom, and the land bee full of wickedness.
19.30: Ye shall keep my Sabbaths and reverence my Sanctuarie: I am the Lord.
19.31: Ye shall not regard them that work with spirites, neither soothsayers: ye shall not seek to them to be defiled by them: I am the Lord your God.
19.32: Thou shalt rise up before the horehead, and honour the person of the old man, and dread thy God: I am the Lord.
19.33: And if a stranger soiourne with thee in your land, ye shall not vex him.
19.34: But the stranger that dwelleth with you, shalbe as one of your selves, and thou shalt love him as thy self: for ye were strangers in the lad of Egypt: I am the Lord your God.
19.35: Ye shall not doe vniustly in iudgement, in line, in weight, or in measure.
19.36: You shall have just balances, true weightes, a true Ephah, and a true Hin. I am the Lord your God, which have brought you out of the land of Egypt.
19.37: Therefore shall ye observe all mine ordinances, and all my iudgements, and doe them: I am the Lord.

20.1: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
20.2: Thou shalt say also to the children of Israel, Whosoever he be of the children of Israel, or of the strangers that dwell in Israel, that giveth his children unto Molech, he shall die the death, ye people of ye land shall stone him to death.
20.3: And I will set my face against that man and cut him off from among his people, because he hath given his children unto Molech, for to defile my Sanctuarie, and to pollute mine holy Name.
20.4: And if the people of the land hide their eyes, and wink at that man when he giveth his children unto Molech, and kill him not,
20.5: Then will I set my face against that man, and against his familie, and will cut him off, and all that go a whoring after him to comit whoredom with Molech, from among their people.
20.6: If any turn after such as work with spirits, and after soothsayers, to go a whoring after them, then will I set my face against that person, and will cut him off from among his people.
20.7: Sanctifie your selves therefore, and be holie, for I am the Lord your God.
20.8: Keep ye therefore mine ordinances, and doe them. I am the Lord which doeth sanctifie you.
20.9: If there be any that curseth his father or his mother, he shall die the death: seeing hee hath cursed his father and his mother, his blood shalbe upon him.
20.10: And the man that committeth adulterie with another mans wife, because he hath comitted adulterie with his neighbours wife, the adulterer and the adulteress shall die the death.
20.11: And the man that lyeth with his fathers wife, because hee hath vncouered his fathers shame, they shall both dye: their blood shalbe upon them.
20.12: Also the man that lyeth with his daughter in law, they both shall dye the death, they have wrought abomination, their blood shalbe upon them.
20.13: The man also that lyeth with the male, as one lyeth with a woman, they have both committed abomination: they shall dye the death, their blood shalbe upon them.
20.14: Likewise he that taketh a wife and her mother, committeth wickedness: they shall burn him and them with fire, that there be no wickednes among you.
20.15: Also the man that lyeth with a beast, shall dye the death, and ye shall slay the beast.
20.16: And if a woman come to any beast, and lye therewith, then thou shalt kill the woman and the beast: they shall die the death, their blood shalbe upon them.
20.17: Also the man that taketh his sister, his fathers daughter, or his mothers daughter, and seeth her shame and she seeth his shame, it is villenie: therefore they shall be cut off in the sight of their people, because he hath vncouered his sisters shame, he shall bear his iniquitie.
20.18: The man also that lyeth with a woman having her disease, and vncouereth her shame, and openeth her fountain, and she open the foutaine of her blood, they shall bee even both cut off from among their people.
20.19: Moreover thou shalt not vncouer the shame of thy mothers sister, nor of thy fathers sister: because he hath vncouered his kin, they shall bear their iniquitie.
20.20: Likewise the man that lyeth with his fathers brothers wife, and vncouereth his vncles shame: they shall bear their iniquitie, and shall die childless.
20.21: So the man that taketh his brothers wife, committeth filthines, because he hath vncouered his brothers shame: they shalbe childles.
20.22: Ye shall keep therefore all mine ordinances and all my iudgements, and doe them, that the land, whither I bring you to dwel therein, spue you not out.
20.23: Wherefore ye shall not walk in the maners of this nation which I cast out before you: for they have committed all these things, therefore I abhorred them.
20.24: But I have said unto you, ye shall inherit their land, and I will give it unto you to possess it, even a land that floweth with milk and honie: I am the Lord your God, which have separated you from other people.
20.25: Therefore shall ye put difference between clean beastes and vncleane, and between vncleane foules and clean: neither shall ye defile your selves with beastes and foules, nor with any creeping thing, that ye ground bringeth forth, which I have separated from you as vncleane.
20.26: Therefore shall ye be holie unto me: for I the Lord am holy, and I have separated you from other people, that ye should be mine.
20.27: And if a man or woman have a spirit of divination, or soothsaying in them, they shall die the death: they shall stone them to death, their blood shalbe upon them.

21.1: And the Lord said unto Moses, Speak unto the Priestes the sonnes of Aaron, and say unto them, Let none be defiled by the dead among his people,
21.2: But by his kinseman that is neere unto him: to wit, by his mother, or by his father, or by his sonne, or by his daughter, or by his brother,
21.3: Or by his sister a maid, that is neere unto him, which hath not had a husband: for her he may lament.
21.4: He shall not lament for the Prince among his people, to pollute him self.
21.5: They shall not make bald partes upon their head, nor shave off the locks of their beard, nor make any cuttings in their flesh.
21.6: They shalbe holy unto their God, and not pollute the name of their God: for the sacrifices of the Lord made by fire, and the bread of their God they doe offer: therefore they shalbe holie.
21.7: They shall not take to wife an whore, or one polluted, neither shall they marrie a woman divorced from her husband: for such one is holy unto his God.
21.8: Thou shalt sanctifie him therefore, for he offereth the bread of thy God: he shall be holy unto thee: for I the Lord, which sanctifie you, am holy.
21.9: If a Priestes daughter fall to play the whore, she polluteth her father: therefore shall she be burnt with fire.
21.10: Also ye hie Priest among his brethren, (upon whose head the anointing oyle was powred, and hath consecrated his hand to put on the garments) shall not vncouer his head, nor rent his clothes,
21.11: Neither shall he goe to any dead bodie, nor make him self vncleane by his father or by his mother,
21.12: Neither shall he goe out of the Sanctuarie, nor pollute the holy place of his God: for the crown of the anoynting oyle of his God is upon him: I am the Lord.
21.13: Also he shall take a maid unto his wife:
21.14: But a widow, or a divorced woman, or a polluted, or an harlot, these shall he not marrie, but shall take a maid of his own people to wife:
21.15: Neyther shall he defile his seed among his people: for I am the Lord which sanctifie him.
21.16: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
21.17: Speak unto Aaron, and say, Whosoever of thy seed in their generations hath any blemishes, shall not prease to offer the bread of his God:
21.18: For whosoever hath any blemish, shall not come neere: as a man blind or lame, or that hath a flat nose, or that hath any misshapen member,
21.19: Or a man that hath a broken foot, or a broken hand,
21.20: Or is crooke backt, or bleare eyed, or hath a blemish in his eye, or be skiruie, or skabbed, or have his stones broken.
21.21: None of the seed of Aaron the Priest that hath a blemish, shall come neere to offer the sacrifices of the Lord made by fire, having a blemish: he shall not prease to offer the bread of his God.
21.22: The bread of his God, even of the most holie, and of the holy shall he eat:
21.23: But he shall not goe in unto the vail, nor come neere the altar, because hee hath a blemish, least he pollute my Sanctuaries: for I am the Lord that sanctifie them.
21.24: Thus spake Moses unto Aaron, and to his sonnes, and to all the children of Israel.

22.1: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
22.2: Speak unto Aaron, and to his sonnes, that they be separated from the holy thinges of the children of Israel, and that they pollute not mine holy name in those things, which they hallow unto me: I am the Lord.
22.3: Say unto them, Whosoever he be of all your seed among your generations after you, that toucheth the holy things which the children of Israel hallow unto the Lord, having his vncleannesse upon him, even that person shall be cut off from my sight: I am the Lord.
22.4: Whosoever also of the seed of Aaron is a leper, or hath a running issue, he shall not eat of the holy things until he be clean: and who so toucheth any that is vncleane, by reason of the dead, or a man whose issue of seed runneth from him,
22.5: Or the man that toucheth any creeping thing, whereby he may be made vncleane, or a man, by whom he may take vncleannesse, whatsoever vncleannesse he hath,
22.6: The person that hath touched such, shall therefore be vncleane until the even, and shall not eat of ye holy things, except he have washed his flesh with water.
22.7: But when the Sunne is down, hee shalbe clean, and shall afterward eat of the holy things: for it is his food.
22.8: Of a beast that dyeth, or is rent with beasts, whereby he may be defiled, hee shall not eat: I am the Lord.
22.9: Let them keep therefore mine ordinance, least they bear their sinne for it, and die for it, if they defile it: I the Lord sanctifie them.
22.10: There shall no stranger also eat of the holie thing, neither the ghest of the Priest, neither shall an hired servant eat of the holie thing:
22.11: But if the Priest bye any with money, he shall eat of it, also he that is borne in his house: they shall eat of his meat.
22.12: If the Priests daughter also be maried unto a stranger, she may not eat of the holy offrings.
22.13: Notwithstanding if the Priests daughter be a widow or divorced, and have no child, but is returned unto her fathers house she shall eat of her fathers bread, as she did in her youth but there shall no stranger eat thereof.
22.14: If a man eat of the holie thing unwittingly, he shall put the fift part thereunto, and give it unto the Priest with the halowed thing.
22.15: So they shall not defile the holy things of the children of Israel, which they offer unto the Lord,
22.16: Neither cause the people to bear the iniquitie of their trespas, while they eat their holy thing: for I the Lord do halowe them.
22.17: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
22.18: Speak unto Aaron, and to his sonnes, and to all the children of Israel, and say unto them, Whosoever he be of the house of Israel, or of the strangers in Israel, that will offer his sacrifice for all their vowes, and for all their free offrings, which they use to offer unto the Lord for a burnt offring,
22.19: Yee shall offer of your free mind a male without blemish of the beeves, of the sheep, or of the goates.
22.20: Ye shall not offer any thing that hath a blemish: for that shall not be acceptable for you.
22.21: And whosoever bringeth a peace offring unto ye Lord to accomplish his vow, or for a free offring, of the beeves, or of the sheep, his free offring shall bee perfect, no blemish shalbe in it.
22.22: Blind, or broken, or maimed, or having a wenne, or skiruie, or skabbed: these shall yee not offer unto the Lord nor make an offring by fire of these upon the altar of the Lord.
22.23: Yet a bullock, or a sheep that hath any member superfluous, or lacking, such mayest thou present for a free offring, but for a vow it shall not be accepted.
22.24: Ye shall not offer unto ye Lord that which is bruised or crushed, or broken, or cut away, neither shall ye make an offring thereof in your land,
22.25: Neither of ye hand of a strager shall ye offer ye bread of your God of any of these, because their corruption is in them, there is a blemish in them: therefore shall they not be accepted for you.
22.26: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
22.27: When a bullock, or a sheep, or a goat shall be brought foorth, it shalbe even seven daies under his damme: and from the eight day forth, it shalbe accepted for a sacrifice made by fire unto the Lord.
22.28: As for the cow or the ewe, yee shall not kill her, and her yong both in one day.
22.29: So when ye will offer a thank offring unto the Lord, ye shall offer willingly.
22.30: The same day it shalbe eaten, yee shall leave none of it until the morowe: I am the Lord.
22.31: Therefore shall ye keep my commandements and do them: for I am the Lord.
22.32: Neither shall ye pollute mine holy Name, but I will be halowed among the children of Israel. I the Lord sanctifie you,
22.33: Which have brought you out of the land of Egypt, to be your God: I am the Lord.

23.1: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
23.2: Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, The feastes of ye Lord which yee shall call ye holie assemblies, even these are my feasts.
23.3: Six daies shall work be done, but in the seventh day shalbe the Sabbath of rest, an holie convocation: ye shall do no work therein, it is the Sabbath of the Lord, in all your dwellings.
23.4: These are the feastes of the Lord, and holie convocations, which yee shall proclaim in their seasons.
23.5: In the first moneth, and in the fourteenth day of the moneth at evening shalbe ye Passeouer of the Lord.
23.6: And on the fifteenth day of this moneth shalbe the feast of vnleauened bread unto the Lord: seven dayes ye shall eat vnleauened bread.
23.7: In the first day yee shall have an holy convocation: ye shall do no servile work therein.
23.8: Also ye shall offer sacrifice made by fire unto the Lord seven daies, and in the seventh day shalbe an holie convocation: ye shall do no servile work therein.
23.9: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
23.10: Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When ye be come into ye land which I give unto you, and reap the harvest thereof, then ye shall bring a sheaf of the first fruites of your harvest unto the Priest,
23.11: And hee shall shake the sheaf before the Lord, that it may be acceptable for you: the morowe after the Sabbath, the Priest shall shake it.
23.12: And that day when yee shake the sheaf, shall yee prepare a lamb without blemish of a yeere old, for a burnt offring unto the Lord:
23.13: And the meat offring thereof shalbe two tenth deales of fine flour mingled with oyle, for a sacrifice made by fire unto ye Lord of sweet sauour. and the drink offring thereof the fourth part of an Hin of wine.
23.14: And ye shall eat neither bread nor parched corn, nor green eares until the self same day that ye have brought an offring unto your God: this shalbe a law for ever in your generations and in all your dwellings.
23.15: Ye shall count also to you from the morowe after the Sabbath, even from the day that yee shall bring the sheaf of the shake offring, seven Sabbaths, they shalbe complete.
23.16: Unto ye morow after the seventh Sabbath shall ye nomber fiftie dayes: then yee shall bring a new meat offring unto the Lord.
23.17: Ye shall bring out of your habitations bread for the shake offring: they shalbe two loaves of two tenth deales of fine flour, which shalbe baken with leaven for first fruites unto the Lord.
23.18: Also yee shall offer with the bread seven lambes without blemish of one yeere old, and a yong bullock and two rams: they shalbe for a burnt offring unto the Lord, with their meat offrings and their drink offrings, for a sacrifice made by fire of a sweet sauour unto the Lord.
23.19: Then ye shall prepare an hee goat for a sinne offring, and two lambes of one yeere old for peace offrings.
23.20: And the Priest shall shake them to and from with the bread of the first fruits before the Lord, and with the two lambes: they shalbe holy to the Lord, for the Priest.
23.21: So ye shall proclayme the same day, that it may be an holie convocation unto you: ye shall doe no servile work therein: it shalbe an ordinance for ever in al your dwellinges, throughout your generations.
23.22: And when you reap the harvest of your land, thou shalt not rid clean the corners of thy field when thou reapest, neither shalt thou make any aftergathering of thy harvest, but shalt leave them unto the poor and to the stranger: I am the Lord your God.
23.23: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
23.24: Speak unto the children of Israel, and say, In the seventh moneth, and in the first day of the moneth shall ye have a Sabbath, for the remembrance of blowing the trumpets, an holy convocation.
23.25: Ye shall do no servile work therein, but offer sacrifice made by fire unto the Lord.
23.26: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
23.27: The tenth also of this seventh moneth shalbe a day of reconciliation: it shalbe an holie convocation unto you, and yee shall humble your soules, and offer sacrifice made by fire unto the Lord.
23.28: And ye shall doe no work that same day: for it is a day of reconciliation, to make an atonement for you before the Lord your God.
23.29: For every person that humbleth not himself that same day, shall even be cut off from his people.
23.30: And every person that shall doe any work that same day, the same person also will I destroy from among his people.
23.31: Ye shall do no maner work therefore: this shalbe a law for ever in your generations, throughout all your dwellings.
23.32: This shalbe unto you a Sabbath of rest, and ye shall humble your soules: in the ninth day of the moneth at even, from even to even shall ye celebrate your Sabbath.
23.33: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
23.34: Speak unto the children of Israel, and say, In the fifteenth day of this seueth moneth shalbe for seven dayes the feast of Tabernacles unto the Lord.
23.35: In the first day shalbe an holie convocation: ye shall do no servile work therein.
23.36: Seven daies ye shall offer sacrifice made by fire unto the Lord, and in the eight day shalbe an holy convocation unto you, and ye shall offer sacrifices made by fire unto the Lord: it is the solemn assemblie, yee shall doe no servile work therein.
23.37: These are the feastes of the Lord (which ye shall call holie convocations) to offer sacrifice made by fire unto the Lord, as burnt offring, and meat offring, sacrifice, and drink offrings, every one upon his day,
23.38: Beside the Sabbaths of the Lord, and beside your giftes, and beside al your vowes, and beside all your free offrings, which ye shall give unto the Lord.
23.39: But in the fifteenth day of the seueth moneth, when ye have gathered in the fruit of the land, ye shall keep an holie feast unto the Lord seven daies: in the first day shalbe a Sabbath: likewise in the eight day shalbe a Sabbath.
23.40: And yee shall take you in the first day the fruit of goodly trees, branches of palm trees, and the boughes of thick trees, and willowes of the brook, and shall reioyce before the Lord your God seven daies.
23.41: So ye shall keep this feast unto the Lord seven daies in the yere, by a perpetual ordinance through your generations: in the seventh moneth shall you keep it.
23.42: Ye shall dwell in boothes seven daies: all that are Israelites borne, shall dwel in boothes,
23.43: That your posterity may know that I have made the children of Israel to dwell in boothes, when I brought them out of the land of Egypt: I am the Lord your God.
23.44: So Moses declared unto the children of Israel the feastes of the Lord.

24.1: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
24.2: Command the children of Israel that they bring unto thee pure oyle olive beaten, for the light, to cause ye lampes to burn continually.
24.3: Without the vail of the Testimonie, in the Tabernacle of the Congregation, shall Aaron dress them, both even and morning before the Lord alwayes: this shalbe a law for ever through your generations.
24.4: He shall dress the lampes upon the pure Candlestick before the Lord perpetually.
24.5: Also thou shalt take fine flour, and bake twelve cakes thereof: two tenth deales shalbe in one cake.
24.6: And thou shalt set them in two rowes, six in a row upon the pure table before the Lord.
24.7: Thou shalt also put pure incense upon the rowes, that in stead of the bread it may bee for a remembrance, and an offering made by fire to the Lord.
24.8: Every Sabbath hee shall put them in rowes before the Lord evermore, receiving them of the children of Israel for an everlasting covenant.
24.9: And the bread shalbe Aarons and his sonnes, and they shall eat it in the holie place: for it is most holie unto him of the offrings of the Lord made by fire by a perpetual ordinance.
24.10: And there went out among the children of Israel the sonne of an Israelitish woman, whose father was an Egyptian: and this sonne of the Israelitish woman, and a man of Israel strove together in the host.
24.11: So the Israelitish womans sonne blasphemed the name of the Lord, and cursed, and they brought him unto Moses (his mothers name also was Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan)
24.12: And they put him in ward, till he told them the mind of the Lord.
24.13: Then the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
24.14: Bring the blasphemer without the host, and let all that heard him, put their handes upon his head, and let all the Congregation stone him.
24.15: And thou shalt speak unto the children of Israel, saying, Whosoever curseth his God, shall bear his sinne.
24.16: And he that blasphemeth the name of the Lord, shalbe put to death: all the Congregation shall stone him to death: aswell the stranger, as he that is borne in the land: when he blasphemeth the name of the Lord, let him beslaine.
24.17: He also that killeth any man, he shall be put to death.
24.18: And he that killeth a beast, he shall restore it, beast for beast.
24.19: Also if a man cause any blemish in his neighbour: as he hath done, so shall it be done to him.
24.20: Breach for breach, eye for eye, tooth for tooth: such a blemish as he hath made in any, such shalbe repayed to him.
24.21: And he that killeth a beast shall restore it: but he that killeth a man shall be slain.
24.22: Ye shall have one law: it shalbe aswel for the stranger as for one borne in the countrey: for I am the Lord your God.
24.23: Then Moses told the children of Israel, and they brought the blasphemer out of the host, and stoned him with stones: so the children of Israel did as the Lord had commanded Moses.

25.1: And the Lord spake unto Moses in mount Sinai, saying,
25.2: Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When ye shall come into the land which I give you, the land shall keep Sabbath unto the Lord.
25.3: Six yeeres thou shalt sow thy field, and six yeeres thou shalt cut thy vineyard, and gather the fruit thereof.
25.4: But the seventh yeere shalbe a Sabbath of rest unto the land: it shall be the Lordes Sabbath: thou shalt neither sow thy field, nor cut thy vineyard.
25.5: That which groweth of it own accord of thy harvest, thou shalt not reap, neither gather the grapes that thou hast left vnlaboured: for it shalbe a yeere of rest unto the land.
25.6: And the rest of the land shall be meat for you, even for thee, and for thy servant, and for thy mayde, and for thy hired servant, and for the stranger that soiourneth with thee:
25.7: And for thy cattell, and for the beastes that are in thy land shall all the encrease thereof be meat.
25.8: Also thou shalt number seven Sabbaths of yeeres unto thee, even seven times seven yeere: and the space of the seven Sabbaths of yeeres will be unto thee nine and fourtie yeere.
25.9: Then thou shalt cause to blow the trumpet of the Jubile in the tenth day of the seventh moneth: even in the day of the reconciliation shall ye make the trumpet blow, throughout all your land.
25.10: And ye shall halowe that yeere, even the fiftieth yeere, and proclaim libertie in the land to all the inhabitants thereof: it shalbe the Jubile unto you, and ye shall return every man unto his possession, and every man shall return unto his familie.
25.11: This fiftieth yeere shalbe a yeere of Jubile unto you: ye shall not sow, neither reap that which groweth of it self, neither gather the grapes thereof, that are left vnlaboured.
25.12: For it is the Jubile, it shall be holy unto you: ye shall eat of the encrease thereof out of the field.
25.13: In the yeere of this Jubile, ye shall return every man unto his possession.
25.14: And when thou sellest ought to thy neighbour, or byest at thy neighbours hand, ye shall not oppress one another:
25.15: But according to the nomber of yeeres after the Jubile thou shalt bye of thy neighbour: also according to the nomber of the yeeres of the reuenues, he shall sell unto thee.
25.16: According to the multitude of yeeres, thou shalt increase the price thereof, and according to the fewness of yeeres, thou shalt abate the price of it: for the nomber of fruites doeth he sell unto thee.
25.17: Oppress not ye therefore any man his neighbour, but thou shalt fear thy God: for I am the Lord your God.
25.18: Wherefore ye shall obey mine ordinances, and keep my lawes, and do them, and ye shall dwell in the land in safetie.
25.19: And the land shall give her fruit, and ye shall eat your fill, and dwell therein in safetie.
25.20: And if ye shall say, What shall we eat the seventh yeere, for we shall not sow, nor gather in our increase?
25.21: I will send my blessing upon you in the sixt yeere, and it shall bring foorth fruit for three yeeres.
25.22: And ye shall sow the eight yeere, and eat of the old fruit until the ninth yeere: until the fruit thereof come, ye shall eat the old.
25.23: Also the land shall not be sold to be cut off from the familie: for the land is mine, and ye be but strangers and soiourners with me.
25.24: Therefore in all the land of your possession ye shall graunt a redemption for the land.
25.25: If thy brother be impoverished, and sell his possession, then his redeemer shall come, even his neere kinsman, and bye out that which his brother sold.
25.26: And if he have no redeemer, but hath gotten and found to bye it out,
25.27: Then shall he count the yeeres of his sale, and restore the ouerplus to the man, to whom he sold it: so shall he return to his possession.
25.28: But if he can not get sufficient to restore to him, then that which is sold, shall remain in the hand of him that hath bought it, until the yere of the Jubile: and in the Jubile it shall come out, and he shall return unto his possession.
25.29: Likewise if a man sell a dwelling house in a walled citie, he may bye it out again within a whole yeere after it is sold: within a yeere may he bye it out.
25.30: But if it be not bought out within ye space of a ful yeere, then the house that is in the walled citie, shalbe stablished, as cut off from the familie, to him that bought it, throughout his generations: it shall not goe out in the Jubile.
25.31: But the houses of villages, which have no walles round about them, shalbe esteemed as the field of the countrey: they may be bought out again, and shall goe out in the Jubile.
25.32: Notwithstanding, the cities of the Levites, and the houses of the cities of their possession, may the Levites redeem at all seasons.
25.33: And if a man purchase of the Levites, the house that was sold, and the citie of their possession shall goe out in the Jubile: for the houses of the cities of the Levites are their possession among the children of Israel.
25.34: But the field of the suburbes of their cities, shall not be sold: for it is their perpetual possession.
25.35: Moreover, if thy brother be impoverished, and fallen in decay with thee, thou shalt relieve him, and as a stranger and soiourner, so shall he live with thee.
25.36: Thou shalt take no vsurie of him, nor vantage, but thou shalt fear thy God, that thy brother may live with thee.
25.37: Thou shalt not give him thy money to vsurie, nor lend him thy vitailes for increase.
25.38: I am the Lord your God, which have brought you out of the land of Egypt, to give you the land of Canaan, and to be your God.
25.39: If thy brother also that dwelleth by thee, be impoverished, and be sold unto thee, thou shalt not compel him to serve as a bond servant,
25.40: But as an hired servant, and as a soiourner he shalbe with thee: he shall serve thee unto the yeere of the Jubile.
25.41: Then shall he depart from thee, both hee, and his children with him, and shall return unto his familie, and unto the possession of his fathers shall he return:
25.42: For they are my servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt: they shall not be sold as bondmen are sold.
25.43: Thou shalt not rule over him cruelly, but shalt fear thy God.
25.44: Thy bond servant also, and thy bond maid, which thou shalt have, shalbe of the heathen that are round about you: of them shall ye bye servants and maydes.
25.45: And moreover of the children of the stragers, that are soiourners among you, of them shall ye bye, and of their families that are with you, which they begat in your land: these shall be your possession.
25.46: So ye shall take them as inheritance for your children after you, to possess them by inheritance, ye shall use their labours for ever: but over your brethren the children of Israel ye shall not rule one over another with crueltie.
25.47: If a soiourner or a stranger dwelling by thee get riches, and thy brother by him be impoverished, and sell him self unto the stranger or soiourner dwelling by thee, or to the stock of the strangers familie,
25.48: After that he is sold, he may be bought out: one of his brethren may bye him out,
25.49: Or his uncle, or his vncles sonne may bye him out, or any of the kindred of his flesh among his familie, may redeem him: either if he can get so much, he may bye him self out.
25.50: Then he shall recken with his byer from the yeere that he was sold to him, unto the yere of Jubile: and the money of his sale shalbe according to the number of yeeres: according to the time of an hyred servant shall he be with him.
25.51: If there be many yeeres behind, according to them he shall give again for his deliverance, of the money that he was bought for.
25.52: If there remain but few yeeres unto the yeere of Jubile, then he shall count with him, and according to his yeeres give again for his redemption.
25.53: He shalbe with him yeere by yeere as an hired servant: he shall not rule cruelly over him in thy sight.
25.54: And if he be not redeemed thus, he shall go out in the yeere of Jubile, he, and his children with him.
25.55: For unto me the children of Israel are servants: they are my servants, who I have brought out of the land of Egypt: I am ye Lord your God.

26.1: Ye shall make you none idoles nor graven image, neither rear you up any pillar, neither shall ye set any image of stone in your land to bow down to it: for I am the Lord your God.
26.2: Ye shall keep my Sabbaths, and reverence my Sanctuarie: I am the Lord.
26.3: If ye walk in mine ordinances, and keep my commandements, and doe them,
26.4: I will then send you rain in due season, and the land shall yelde her increase, and the trees of the field shall give her fruit.
26.5: And your threshing shall reach unto the vintage, and the vintage shall reach unto sowing time, and you shall eat your bread in plenteousness, and dwell in your land safely.
26.6: And I will send peace in the land, and ye shall sleep and none shall make you afraid: also I will rid evil beastes out of the land, and the sword shall not go through your land.
26.7: Also ye shall chase your enemies, and they shall fall before you upon the sword.
26.8: And five of you shall chase an hundreth, and an hundreth of you shall put ten thousand to flight, and your enemies shall fall before you upon the sword.
26.9: For I will have respect unto you, and make you encrease, and multiplie you, and establish my covenant with you.
26.10: Ye shall eat also old store, and cary out old because of the new.
26.11: And I will set my Tabernacle among you, and my soul shall not lothe you.
26.12: Also I will walk among you, and I wil be your God, and ye shalbe my people.
26.13: I am the Lord your God which have brought you out of the land of Egypt, that yee should not be their bondmen, and I have broken ye bonds of your yoke, and made you goe upright.
26.14: But if ye will not obey me, nor do all these commandements,
26.15: And if ye shall despise mine ordinances, either if your soul abhorre my lawes, so that yee will not do all my commandements, but break my covenant,
26.16: Then wil I also do this unto you, I wil appoint over you fearefulnes, a consumption, and the burning ague to consume the eyes, and make the heart heauie, and you shall sow your seed in vain: for your enemies shall eat it:
26.17: And I will set my face against you, and ye shall fal before your enemies, and they that hate you, shall raigne over you, and yee shall flee when none pursueth you.
26.18: And if ye wil not for these things obey me, then wil I punish you seven times more, according to your sinnes,
26.19: And I wil break the pride of your power, and I will make your heaven as yron, and your earth as brass:
26.20: And your strength shalbe spent in vain: neither shall your land give her increase, neither shall the trees of the land give their fruit.
26.21: And if ye walk stubburnly against me, and will not obey mee, I will then bring seven times more plagues upon you, according to your sinnes.
26.22: I will also send wild beastes upon you, which shall spoyle you, and destroy your cattell, and make you few in number: so your hye waies shalbe desolate.
26.23: Yet if by these ye will not be reformed by me, but walk stubburnly against me,
26.24: Then wil I also walk stubburnly against you, and I will smite you yet seven times for your sinnes:
26.25: And I wil send a sword upon you, that shall avenge the quarel of my covenant: and when ye are gathered in your cities, I wil send the pestilence among you, and ye shall be delivered into the hand of the enemie.
26.26: When I shall break the staff of your bread, then ten women shall bake your bread in one oven, and they shall deliver your bread again by weight, and ye shall eat, but not be satisfied.
26.27: Yet if ye will not for this obey mee, but walk against me stubburnly,
26.28: Then will I walk stubburnly in mine anger against you, and I will also chastice you seven times more according to your sinnes.
26.29: And ye shall eat ye flesh of your sonnes, and the flesh of your daughters shall ye deuoure.
26.30: I will also destroy your hye places, and cut away your images, and cast your carkeises upon the bodies of your idoles, and my soul shall abhorre you.
26.31: And I will make your cities desolate, and bring your Sanctuarie unto nought, and will not smell the sauour of your sweet odours.
26.32: I will also bring the land unto a wildernes, and your enemies, which dwell therein, shalbe astonished thereat.
26.33: Also I wil scatter you among the heathen, and will draw out a sword after you, and your land shalbe waste, and your cities shalbe desolate.
26.34: Then shall the land inioy her Sabbaths, as long as it lieth void, and yee shalbe in your enemies land: then shall the land rest, and enioy her Sabbaths.
26.35: All the dayes that it lieth void, it shall rest, because it did not rest in your Sabbaths, when ye dwelt upon it.
26.36: And upon them that are left of you, I will send even a faintnes into their hearts in ye land of their enemies, and the sound of a leafeshaken shall chase them, and they shall flee as fleeing from a sword, and they shall fall, no man pursuing them.
26.37: They shall fall also one upon another, as before a sword, though none pursue them, and ye shall not be able to stand before your enemies:
26.38: And ye shall perish among the heathen, and the land of your enemies shall eat you up.
26.39: And they that are left of you, shall pine away for their iniquitie, in your enemies landes, and for the iniquities of their fathers shall they pine away with them also.
26.40: Then they shall confess their iniquitie, and the wickednes of their fathers for their trespass, which they have trespassed against mee, and also because they have walked stubburnly against me.
26.41: Therefore I wil walk stubburnly against them, and bring them into the land of their enemies: so then their uncircumcised hearts shalbe humbled, and then they shalt willingly bear the punishment of their iniquitie.
26.42: Then I will remember my covenant with Iaakob, and my covenant also with Izhak, and also my covenant with Abraham will I remember, and will remember the land.
26.43: The land also in the mean season shalbe left of them, and shall enioye her Sabbaths while she lieth waste without them, but they shall willingly suffer the punishment of their iniquitie, because they despised my lawes, and because their soul abhorred mine ordinances.
26.44: Yet notwithstanding this, when they shalbe in the land of their enemies, I wil not cast them away, neither will I abhorre them, to destroy them utterly, nor to break my covenant with them: for I am the Lord their God:
26.45: But I will remember for them the covenant of old when I brought them out of ye land of Egypt in the sight of the heathen that I might be their God: I am the Lord.
26.46: These are the ordinances, and the iudgements, and the lawes, which the Lord made between him, and the children of Israel in mount Sinai, by the hand of Moses.

27.1: Moreover the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
27.2: Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, If any man shall make a vow of a person unto the Lord, by thy estimation,
27.3: Then thy estimation shall bee thus: a male from twentie yeere old unto sixty yeere old shalbe by thy estimation even fifty shekels of silver, after the shekel of the Sanctuarie.
27.4: But if it be a female, then thy valuation shall be thirtie shekels.
27.5: And from five yere old to twentie yere old thy valuation shall be for the male twentie shekels, and for the female ten shekels.
27.6: But from a moneth old unto five yere old, thy price of the male shall bee five shekels of silver, and thy price of the female, three shekels of silver.
27.7: And from sixty yeere old and above, if he be a male, then thy price shalbe fifteen shekels, and for the female ten shekels.
27.8: But if he be poorer then thou hast esteemed him, then shall hee present himself before the Priest, and the Priest shall value him, according to the abilitie of him that vowed, so shall the Priest value him.
27.9: And if it be a beast, whereof men bring an offering unto the Lord, all that one giveth of such unto the Lord, shalbe holy.
27.10: He shall not alter it nor change it, a good for a bad, nor a bad for a good: and if hee change beast for beast, then both this and that, which was changed for it, shall be holy.
27.11: And if it be any vncleane beast, of which men do not offer a sacrifice unto the Lord, hee shall then present the beast before the Priest.
27.12: And the Priest shall value it, whether it be good or bad: and as thou valuest it, which art the Priest, so shall it bee.
27.13: But if he will bye it again, then hee shall give the fift part of it more, above thy valuation.
27.14: Also whe a man shall dedicate his house to be holy unto the Lord, then the Priest shall value it, whether it be good or bad, and as ye Priest shall prise it, so shall the value be.
27.15: But if he that sanctified it, will redeem his house, then hee shall give thereto the fift part of money more then thy estimation, and it shalbe his.
27.16: If also a man dedicate to the Lord any ground of his inheritance, then shalt thou esteem it according to the seed therof: an Homer of barlie seed shalbe at fiftie shekels of silver.
27.17: If he dedicate his field immediatly from the yeere of Jubile, it shall bee worth as thou doest esteem it.
27.18: But if hee dedicate his field after the Jubile, then the Priest shall recken him the money according to ye yeeres that remain unto the yere of Jubile, and it shalbe abated by thy estimation.
27.19: And if he that dedicateth it, will redeem the field, then he shall put the fift part of the price, that thou esteemedst it at, thereunto, and it shall remain his.
27.20: And if he will not redeem the field, but the Priest sell the field to another man, it shalbe redeemed no more.
27.21: But the field shalbe holy to the Lord, whe it goeth out in the Jubile, as a field separate from common uses: the possession thereof shall be the Priests.
27.22: If a man also dedicate unto ye Lord a field which he hath bought, which is not of the groud of his inheritance,
27.23: Then the Priest shall set the price to him, as thou esteemest it, unto the yeere of Jubile, and he shall give thy price the same day, as a thing holy unto the Lord.
27.24: But in the yeere of Jubile, the field shall return unto him, of whom it was bought: to him, I say, whose inheritance the land was.
27.25: And all thy valuation shall bee according to the shekel of the Sanctuarie: a shekel conteyneth twenty gerahs.
27.26: Notwithstanding the first borne of the beastes, because it is the Lordes first borne, none shall dedicate such, be it bullock, or sheep; for it is the Lords.
27.27: But if it be an vncleane beast, then he shall redeem it by thy valuation, and give the fift part more thereto: and if it be not redeemed, then it shalbe sold, according to thy estimation.
27.28: Notwithstanding, nothing separate from the common use that a man doeth separate unto the Lord of all that he hath (whether it bee man or beast, or land of his inheritance) may be sold nor redeemed: for every thing separate from the common use is most holy unto the Lord.
27.29: Nothing separate from the common use, which shall be separate from man, shalbe redeemed, but dye the death.
27.30: Also all the tithe of the land both of the seed of the ground, and of the fruit of the trees is the Lords: it is holy to the Lord.
27.31: But if a man will redeem any of his tithe, he shall add the fift part thereto.
27.32: And every tithe of bullock, and of sheep, and of all that goeth under the rod, the tenth shalbe holy unto the Lord.
27.33: He shall not look if it be good or bad, neither shall he change it: els if he change it, both it, and that it was changed withal, shalbe holy, and it shall not be redeemed.
27.34: These are the commandements which the Lord commanded by Moses unto the children of Israel in mount Sinai.
